<hr>
<br>
<pre>public class <span class="typeNameLabel">TxReport</span>
extends <a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true" title="class or interface in java.lang">Object</a></pre>
<div class="block">This class wraps a raw pointer than points to a Rust `TxReport` object.
 </p>
 The `TxReport` contains information about a successful Mentat transaction.
 </p>
 This information includes:
 <ul>
     <li>`txId` - the identifier for the transaction.</li>
     <li>`txInstant` - the time that the transaction occured.</li>
     <li>a map of temporary identifiers provided in the transaction and the `Entid`s that they were mapped to.</li>
 </ul>
 </p>
 Access an `Entid` for a temporary identifier that was provided in the transaction can be done through `entid(String:)`.
 </p>
 <pre><code>
 TxReport report = mentat.transact("[[:db/add "a" :foo/boolean true]]");
 long aEntid = report.getEntidForTempId("a");
</code></pre></div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="subTitle">org.mozilla.mentat</div>
<h2 title="Class TypedValue" class="title">Class TypedValue</h2>
</div>
<div class="contentContainer">
<ul class="inheritance">
<li><a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true" title="class or interface in java.lang">java.lang.Object</a></li>
<li>
<ul class="inheritance">
<li>org.mozilla.mentat.TypedValue</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="description">
<ul class="blockList">
<li class="blockList">
<dl>
<dt>All Implemented Interfaces:</dt>
<dd><a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html?is-external=true" title="class or interface in java.lang">AutoCloseable</a></dd>
</dl>
<hr>
<br>
<pre>public class <span class="typeNameLabel">TypedValue</span>
extends <a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/java/lang/Object.html?is-external=true" title="class or interface in java.lang">Object</a></pre>
<div class="block">A wrapper around Mentat's `TypedValue` Rust object. This class wraps a raw pointer to a Rust `TypedValue`
 struct and provides accessors to the values according to expected result type.
 </p>
 As the FFI functions for fetching values are consuming, this class keeps a copy of the result internally after
 fetching so that the value can be referenced several times.
 </p>
 Also, due to the consuming nature of the FFI layer, this class also manages it's raw pointer, nilling it after calling the
 FFI conversion function so that the underlying base class can manage cleanup.</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>

FILE: docs/apis/0.7/rust/storage.js
================================================
var resourcesSuffix = "";
/*!
 * Copyright 2018 The Rust Project Developers. See the COPYRIGHT
 * file at the top-level directory of this distribution and at
 * http://rust-lang.org/COPYRIGHT.
 *
 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 <LICENSE-APACHE or
 * http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0> or the MIT license
 * <LICENSE-MIT or http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT>, at your
 * option. This file may not be copied, modified, or distributed
 * except according to those terms.
 */

var currentTheme = document.getElementById("themeStyle");
var mainTheme = document.getElementById("mainThemeStyle");

var savedHref = [];

function onEach(arr, func) {
    if (arr && arr.length > 0 && func) {
        for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
            if (func(arr[i]) === true) {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
}

function updateLocalStorage(name, value) {
    if (typeof(Storage) !== "undefined") {
        localStorage[name] = value;
    } else {
        // No Web Storage support so we do nothing
    }
}

function getCurrentValue(name) {
    if (typeof(Storage) !== "undefined" && localStorage[name] !== undefined) {
        return localStorage[name];
    }
    return null;
}

function switchTheme(styleElem, mainStyleElem, newTheme) {
    var fullBasicCss = "rustdoc" + resourcesSuffix + ".css";
    var fullNewTheme = newTheme + resourcesSuffix + ".css";
    var newHref = mainStyleElem.href.replace(fullBasicCss, fullNewTheme);

    if (styleElem.href === newHref) {
        return;
    }

    var found = false;
    if (savedHref.length === 0) {
        onEach(document.getElementsByTagName("link"), function(el) {
            savedHref.push(el.href);
        });
    }
    onEach(savedHref, function(el) {
        if (el === newHref) {
            found = true;
            return true;
        }
    });
    if (found === true) {
        styleElem.href = newHref;
        updateLocalStorage('rustdoc-theme', newTheme);
    }
}

switchTheme(currentTheme, mainTheme, getCurrentValue('rustdoc-theme') || 'light');

FILE: docs/apis/0.7/rust/theme.js

var themes = document.getElementById("theme-choices");
var themePicker = document.getElementById("theme-picker");
themePicker.onclick = function() {
    if (themes.style.display === "block") {
        themes.style.display = "none";
        themePicker.style.borderBottomRightRadius = "3px";
        themePicker.style.borderBottomLeftRadius = "3px";
    } else {
        themes.style.display = "block";
        themePicker.style.borderBottomRightRadius = "0";
        themePicker.style.borderBottomLeftRadius = "0";
    }
};
["dark","light"].forEach(function(item) {
    var but = document.createElement('button');
    but.innerHTML = item;
    but.onclick = function(el) {
        switchTheme(currentTheme, mainTheme, item);
    };
    themes.appendChild(but);
});

This is the most efficient time zone when you don't need the local time.
It is also used as an offset (which is also a dummy type).</p>
<p>Using the <a href="./trait.TimeZone.html"><code>TimeZone</code></a> methods

instances.</p>

            <div class="infos">
                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Accepted types are: <code>fn</code>, <code>mod</code>,
                    <code>struct</code>, <code>enum</code>,
                    <code>trait</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>macro</code>,
                    and <code>const</code>.

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../index.html'>edn</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>entities</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>TxFunction</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/entities.rs.html#83-85' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct TxFunction {
    pub op: <a class="struct" href="../../edn/symbols/struct.PlainSymbol.html" title="struct edn::symbols::PlainSymbol">PlainSymbol</a>,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A &quot;transaction function&quot; that exposes some value determined by the current transaction.  The
prototypical example is the current transaction ID, <code>(transaction-tx)</code>.</p>
<p>A natural next step might be to expose the current transaction instant <code>(transaction-instant)</code>,
but that's more difficult: the transaction itself can set the transaction instant (with some
restrictions), so the transaction function must be late-binding.  Right now, that's difficult to
arrange in the transactor.</p>
<p>In the future, we might accept arguments; for example, perhaps we might expose <code>(ancestor (transaction-tx) n)</code> to find the n-th ancestor of the current transaction.  If we do accept
arguments, then the special case of <code>(lookup-ref a v)</code> should be handled as part of the
generalization.</p>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>

            <div class="infos">
                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Accepted types are: <code>fn</code>, <code>mod</code>,
                    <code>struct</code>, <code>enum</code>,
                    <code>trait</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>macro</code>,
                    and <code>const</code>.
                </p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='../index.html'>edn</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>query</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>FindSpec</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/query.rs.html#654-670' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum FindSpec {
    FindRel(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;),
    FindColl(<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>),
    FindTuple(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;),
    FindScalar(<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A definition of the first part of a find query: the
<code>[:find ?foo ?bar…]</code> bit.</p>
<p>There are four different kinds of find specs, allowing you to query for
a single value, a collection of values from different entities, a single
tuple (relation), or a collection of tuples.</p>
<p>Examples:</p>

<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">


  <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">elements</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="macro">vec</span><span class="macro">!</span>[
    <span class="ident">Element</span>::<span class="ident">Variable</span>(<span class="ident">Variable</span>::<span class="ident">from_valid_name</span>(<span class="string">&quot;?foo&quot;</span>)),
    <span class="ident">Element</span>::<span class="ident">Variable</span>(<span class="ident">Variable</span>::<span class="ident">from_valid_name</span>(<span class="string">&quot;?bar&quot;</span>)),
  ];
  <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">rel</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">FindSpec</span>::<span class="ident">FindRel</span>(<span class="ident">elements</span>);

  <span class="kw">if</span> <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">FindSpec</span>::<span class="ident">FindRel</span>(<span class="ident">elements</span>) <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">rel</span> {
    <span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="number">2</span>, <span class="ident">elements</span>.<span class="ident">len</span>());
  }
</pre>
</div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>
                   Variants<a href='#variants' class='anchor'></a></h2>
<span id="variant.FindRel" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindRel" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindRel.v' class='invisible'><code>FindRel(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns an array of arrays, represented as a single array with length a multiple of width.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindColl" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindColl" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindColl.v' class='invisible'><code>FindColl(<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns an array of scalars, usually homogeneous.
This is equivalent to mapping over the results of a <code>FindRel</code>,
returning the first value of each.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindTuple" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindTuple" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindTuple.v' class='invisible'><code>FindTuple(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns a single tuple: a heterogeneous array of scalars. Equivalent to
taking the first result from a <code>FindRel</code>.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindScalar" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindScalar" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindScalar.v' class='invisible'><code>FindScalar(<a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns a single scalar value. Equivalent to taking the first result
from a <code>FindColl</code>.</p>
</div>
                    <h2 id='methods' class='small-section-header'>
                      Methods<a href='#methods' class='anchor'></a>
                    </h2>
                <h3 id='impl' class='impl'><span class='in-band'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>impl <a class="enum" href="../../edn/query/enum.FindSpec.html" title="enum edn::query::FindSpec">FindSpec</a></code><a href='#impl' class='anchor'></a></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/query.rs.html#673-725' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></td></tr></tbody></table></h3><div class='docblock'><p>Returns true if the provided <code>FindSpec</code> returns at most one result.</p>
</div><div class='impl-items'><h4 id='method.is_unit_limited' class="method"><span id='is_unit_limited.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.is_unit_limited' class='fnname'>is_unit_limited</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/query.rs.html#674-682' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><h4 id='method.expected_column_count' class="method"><span id='expected_column_count.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.expected_column_count' class='fnname'>expected_column_count</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/query.rs.html#684-691' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><h4 id='method.requires_distinct' class="method"><span id='requires_distinct.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.requires_distinct' class='fnname'>requires_distinct</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/query.rs.html#712-714' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><div class='docblock'><p>Returns true if the provided <code>FindSpec</code> cares about distinct results.</p>
<p>I use the words &quot;cares about&quot; because find is generally defined in terms of producing distinct
results at the Datalog level.</p>
<p>Two of the find specs (scalar and tuple) produce only a single result. Those don't need to be
run with <code>SELECT DISTINCT</code>, because we're only consuming a single result. Those queries will be
run with <code>LIMIT 1</code>.</p>
<p>Additionally, some projections cannot produce duplicate results: <code>[:find (max ?x) …]</code>, for
example.</p>
<p>This function gives us the hook to add that logic when we're ready.</p>
<p>Beyond this, <code>DISTINCT</code> is not always needed. For example, in some kinds of accumulation or
sampling projections we might not need to do it at the SQL level because we're consuming into
a dupe-eliminating data structure like a Set, or we know that a particular query cannot produce
duplicate results.</p>
</div><h4 id='method.columns' class="method"><div class="important-traits"><div class='tooltip'>ⓘ<span class='tooltiptext'>Important traits for <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>&lt;R&gt;</span></div><div class="content hidden"><h3 class="important">Important traits for <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>&lt;R&gt;</h3><code class="content"><span class="where fmt-newline">impl&lt;R&gt; <a class="trait" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html" title="trait std::io::Read">Read</a> for <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>&lt;R&gt;     Placeholder,
    Variable(<a class="struct" href="../../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>),
    Entid(<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>),
    Ident(<a class="type" href="../../edn/value_rc/type.ValueRc.html" title="type edn::value_rc::ValueRc">ValueRc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../../edn/symbols/struct.Keyword.html" title="struct edn::symbols::Keyword">Keyword</a>&gt;),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>e, a, tx can't be values -- no strings, no floats -- and so
they can only be variables, entity IDs, ident keywords, or
placeholders.
This encoding allows us to represent integers that aren't
entity IDs. That'll get filtered out in the context of the
database.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='../index.html'>edn</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>query</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>UnifyVars</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/query.rs.html#884-910' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum UnifyVars {
    Implicit,
    Explicit(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/set/struct.BTreeSet.html" title="struct alloc::btree::set::BTreeSet">BTreeSet</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>&gt;),
}</pre></div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>
                   Variants<a href='#variants' class='anchor'></a></h2>
<span id="variant.Implicit" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.Implicit" class="anchor field"></a><span id='Implicit.v' class='invisible'><code>Implicit</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>Implicit</code> means the variables in an <code>or</code> or <code>not</code> are derived from the enclosed pattern.
DataScript regards these vars as 'free': these variables don't need to be bound by the
enclosing environment.</p>
<p>Datomic's documentation implies that all implicit variables are required:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Datomic will attempt to push the or clause down until all necessary variables are bound,
and will throw an exception if that is not possible.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>but that would render top-level <code>or</code> expressions (as used in Datomic's own examples!)
impossible, so we assume that this is an error in the documentation.</p>
<p>All contained 'arms' in an <code>or</code> with implicit variables must bind the same vars.</p>
</div><span id="variant.Explicit" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.Explicit" class="anchor field"></a><span id='Explicit.v' class='invisible'><code>Explicit(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/set/struct.BTreeSet.html" title="struct alloc::btree::set::BTreeSet">BTreeSet</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>Explicit</code> means the variables in an <code>or-join</code> or <code>not-join</code> are explicitly listed,
specified with <code>required-vars</code> syntax.</p>
<p>DataScript parses these as free, but allows (incorrectly) the use of more complicated
<code>rule-vars</code> syntax.</p>
<p>Only the named variables will be unified with the enclosing query.</p>
<p>Every 'arm' in an <code>or-join</code> must mention the entire set of explicit vars.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../index.html'>edn</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>symbols</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>Keyword</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/symbols.rs.html#72' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct Keyword(_);</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A keyword is a symbol, optionally with a namespace, that prints with a leading colon.
This concept is imported from Clojure, as it features in EDN and the query
syntax that we use.</p>
<p>Clojure's constraints are looser than ours, allowing empty namespaces or
names:</p>
<pre><code class="language-clojure">user=&gt; (keyword &quot;&quot; &quot;&quot;)
:/
user=&gt; (keyword &quot;foo&quot; &quot;&quot;)
:foo/
user=&gt; (keyword &quot;&quot; &quot;bar&quot;)
:/bar
</code></pre>
<p>We think that's nonsense, so we only allow keywords like <code>:bar</code> and <code>:foo/bar</code>,
with both namespace and main parts containing no whitespace and no colon or slash:</p>

<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">
<span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">bar</span>     <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span>::<span class="ident">plain</span>(<span class="string">&quot;bar&quot;</span>);                         <span class="comment">// :bar</span>
<span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">foo_bar</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span>::<span class="ident">namespaced</span>(<span class="string">&quot;foo&quot;</span>, <span class="string">&quot;bar&quot;</span>);        <span class="comment">// :foo/bar</span>
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;bar&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">bar</span>.<span class="ident">name</span>());
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="prelude-val">None</span>, <span class="ident">bar</span>.<span class="ident">namespace</span>());
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;bar&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">foo_bar</span>.<span class="ident">name</span>());
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="prelude-val">Some</span>(<span class="string">&quot;foo&quot;</span>), <span class="ident">foo_bar</span>.<span class="ident">namespace</span>());</pre>
<p>If you're not sure whether your input is well-formed, you should use a
parser or a reader function first to validate. TODO: implement <code>read</code>.</p>
<p>Callers are expected to follow these rules:
http://www.clojure.org/reference/reader#_symbols</p>
<p>Future: fast equality (interning?) for keywords.</p>
</div>

<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/symbols.rs.html#190-192' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><div class='docblock'><p>Whether this <code>Keyword</code> should be interpreted in reverse order. For example,
the two following snippets are identical:</p>
<pre><code class="language-edn">[?y :person/friend ?x]
[?x :person/hired ?y]

[?y :person/friend ?x]
[?y :person/_hired ?x]
</code></pre>

<span class="macro">assert</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">Keyword</span>::<span class="ident">namespaced</span>(<span class="string">&quot;foo&quot;</span>, <span class="string">&quot;_bar&quot;</span>).<span class="ident">is_backward</span>());</pre>

</div><h4 id='method.is_namespaced' class="method"><span id='is_namespaced.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.is_namespaced' class='fnname'>is_namespaced</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/symbols.rs.html#210-212' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><h4 id='method.to_reversed' class="method"><span id='to_reversed.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.to_reversed' class='fnname'>to_reversed</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="struct" href="../../edn/symbols/struct.Keyword.html" title="struct edn::symbols::Keyword">Keyword</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/symbols.rs.html#232-234' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><div class='docblock'><p>Returns a <code>Keyword</code> with the same namespace and a
'backward' name. See <code>symbols::Keyword::is_backward</code>.</p>
<p>Returns a forward name if passed a reversed keyword; i.e., this
function is its own inverse.</p>
<h1 id="examples-3" class="section-header"><a href="#examples-3">Examples</a></h1>
<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">
<span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">nsk</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span>::<span class="ident">namespaced</span>(<span class="string">&quot;foo&quot;</span>, <span class="string">&quot;bar&quot;</span>);
<span class="macro">assert</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="op">!</span><span class="ident">nsk</span>.<span class="ident">is_backward</span>());
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;:foo/bar&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">nsk</span>.<span class="ident">to_string</span>());

<span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">reversed</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">nsk</span>.<span class="ident">to_reversed</span>();
<span class="macro">assert</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">reversed</span>.<span class="ident">is_backward</span>());
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;:foo/_bar&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">reversed</span>.<span class="ident">to_string</span>());</pre>
</div><h4 id='method.unreversed' class="method"><span id='unreversed.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.unreversed' class='fnname'>unreversed</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../../edn/symbols/struct.Keyword.html" title="struct edn::symbols::Keyword">Keyword</a>&gt;</code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../../src/edn/symbols.rs.html#249-255' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><div class='docblock'><p>If this <code>Keyword</code> is 'backward' (see <code>symbols::Keyword::is_backward</code>),
return <code>Some('forward name')</code>; otherwise, return <code>None</code>.</p>
<h1 id="examples-4" class="section-header"><a href="#examples-4">Examples</a></h1>
<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">

            <div class="infos">
                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>Binding</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#231-235' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum Binding {
    Scalar(<a class="enum" href="../mentat/enum.TypedValue.html" title="enum mentat::TypedValue">TypedValue</a>),
    Vec(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/arc/struct.Arc.html" title="struct alloc::arc::Arc">Arc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat/enum.Binding.html" title="enum mentat::Binding">Binding</a>&gt;&gt;),
    Map(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/arc/struct.Arc.html" title="struct alloc::arc::Arc">Arc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../mentat_core/types/struct.StructuredMap.html" title="struct mentat_core::types::StructuredMap">StructuredMap</a>&gt;),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The values bound in a query specification can be:</p>
<ul>
<li>Vecs of structured values, for multi-valued component attributes or nested expressions.</li>
<li>Single structured values, for single-valued component attributes or nested expressions.</li>
<li>Single typed values, for simple attributes.</li>
</ul>
<p>The <code>Binding</code> enum defines these three options.</p>
<p>Datomic also supports structured inputs; at present Mentat does not, but this type
would also serve that purpose.</p>
<p>Note that maps are not ordered, and so <code>Binding</code> is neither <code>Ord</code> nor <code>PartialOrd</code>.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>FindSpec</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#654-670' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum FindSpec {
    FindRel(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;),
    FindColl(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>),
    FindTuple(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;),
    FindScalar(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A definition of the first part of a find query: the
<code>[:find ?foo ?bar…]</code> bit.</p>
<p>There are four different kinds of find specs, allowing you to query for
a single value, a collection of values from different entities, a single
tuple (relation), or a collection of tuples.</p>
<p>Examples:</p>

<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">


  <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">elements</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="macro">vec</span><span class="macro">!</span>[
    <span class="ident">Element</span>::<span class="ident">Variable</span>(<span class="ident">Variable</span>::<span class="ident">from_valid_name</span>(<span class="string">&quot;?foo&quot;</span>)),
    <span class="ident">Element</span>::<span class="ident">Variable</span>(<span class="ident">Variable</span>::<span class="ident">from_valid_name</span>(<span class="string">&quot;?bar&quot;</span>)),
  ];
  <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">rel</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">FindSpec</span>::<span class="ident">FindRel</span>(<span class="ident">elements</span>);

  <span class="kw">if</span> <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">FindSpec</span>::<span class="ident">FindRel</span>(<span class="ident">elements</span>) <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">rel</span> {
    <span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="number">2</span>, <span class="ident">elements</span>.<span class="ident">len</span>());
  }
</pre>
</div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>
                   Variants<a href='#variants' class='anchor'></a></h2>
<span id="variant.FindRel" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindRel" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindRel.v' class='invisible'><code>FindRel(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns an array of arrays, represented as a single array with length a multiple of width.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindColl" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindColl" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindColl.v' class='invisible'><code>FindColl(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns an array of scalars, usually homogeneous.
This is equivalent to mapping over the results of a <code>FindRel</code>,
returning the first value of each.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindTuple" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindTuple" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindTuple.v' class='invisible'><code>FindTuple(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns a single tuple: a heterogeneous array of scalars. Equivalent to
taking the first result from a <code>FindRel</code>.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindScalar" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindScalar" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindScalar.v' class='invisible'><code>FindScalar(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns a single scalar value. Equivalent to taking the first result
from a <code>FindColl</code>.</p>
</div>
                    <h2 id='methods' class='small-section-header'>
                      Methods<a href='#methods' class='anchor'></a>

</div><div class='impl-items'><h4 id='method.is_unit_limited' class="method"><span id='is_unit_limited.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.is_unit_limited' class='fnname'>is_unit_limited</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#674-682' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><h4 id='method.expected_column_count' class="method"><span id='expected_column_count.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.expected_column_count' class='fnname'>expected_column_count</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#684-691' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><h4 id='method.requires_distinct' class="method"><span id='requires_distinct.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.requires_distinct' class='fnname'>requires_distinct</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#712-714' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><div class='docblock'><p>Returns true if the provided <code>FindSpec</code> cares about distinct results.</p>
<p>I use the words &quot;cares about&quot; because find is generally defined in terms of producing distinct
results at the Datalog level.</p>
<p>Two of the find specs (scalar and tuple) produce only a single result. Those don't need to be
run with <code>SELECT DISTINCT</code>, because we're only consuming a single result. Those queries will be
run with <code>LIMIT 1</code>.</p>
<p>Additionally, some projections cannot produce duplicate results: <code>[:find (max ?x) …]</code>, for
example.</p>
<p>This function gives us the hook to add that logic when we're ready.</p>
<p>Beyond this, <code>DISTINCT</code> is not always needed. For example, in some kinds of accumulation or
sampling projections we might not need to do it at the SQL level because we're consuming into
a dupe-eliminating data structure like a Set, or we know that a particular query cannot produce
duplicate results.</p>

            <div class="infos">
                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>

                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/lib.rs.html#123-167' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct Attribute {
    pub value_type: <a class="enum" href="../mentat/enum.ValueType.html" title="enum mentat::ValueType">ValueType</a>,
    pub multival: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a>,
    pub unique: <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat/vocabulary/attribute/enum.Unique.html" title="enum mentat::vocabulary::attribute::Unique">Unique</a>&gt;,
    pub index: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a>,
    pub fulltext: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a>,
    pub component: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a>,
    pub no_history: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a>,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A Mentat schema attribute has a value type and several other flags determining how assertions
with the attribute are interpreted.</p>
<p>TODO: consider packing this into a bitfield or similar.</p>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.value_type" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.value_type" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="value_type.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>value_type: <a class="enum" href="../mentat/enum.ValueType.html" title="enum mentat::ValueType">ValueType</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The associated value type, i.e., <code>:db/valueType</code>?</p>
</div><span id="structfield.multival" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.multival" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="multival.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>multival: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is multi-valued, i.e., it is <code>:db/cardinality :db.cardinality/many</code>.  <code>false</code> if this attribute is single-valued (the default), i.e., it
is <code>:db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.unique" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.unique" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="unique.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>unique: <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat/vocabulary/attribute/enum.Unique.html" title="enum mentat::vocabulary::attribute::Unique">Unique</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>None</code> if this attribute is neither unique-value nor unique-identity.</p>
<p><code>Some(attribute::Unique::Value)</code> if this attribute is unique-value, i.e., it is <code>:db/unique :db.unique/value</code>.</p>
<p><em>Unique-value</em> means that there is at most one assertion with the attribute and a
particular value in the datom store.  Unique-value attributes can be used in lookup-refs.</p>
<p><code>Some(attribute::Unique::Identity)</code> if this attribute is unique-identity, i.e., it is <code>:db/unique :db.unique/identity</code>.</p>
<p>Unique-identity attributes always have value type <code>Ref</code>.</p>
<p><em>Unique-identity</em> means that the attribute is <em>unique-value</em> and that they can be used in
lookup-refs and will automatically upsert where appropriate.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.index" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.index" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="index.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>index: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is automatically indexed, i.e., it is <code>:db/indexing true</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.fulltext" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.fulltext" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="fulltext.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>fulltext: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is automatically fulltext indexed, i.e., it is <code>:db/fulltext true</code>.</p>
<p>Fulltext attributes always have string values.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.component" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.component" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="component.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>component: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is a component, i.e., it is <code>:db/isComponent true</code>.</p>
<p>Component attributes always have value type <code>Ref</code>.</p>
<p>They are used to compose entities from component sub-entities: they are fetched recursively
by pull expressions, and they are automatically recursively deleted where appropriate.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.no_history" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.no_history" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="no_history.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>no_history: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute doesn't require history to be kept, i.e., it is <code>:db/noHistory true</code>.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>QueryInputs</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">

               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_query_algebrizer/clauses/inputs.rs.html#33-36' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct QueryInputs { /* fields omitted */ }</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Define the inputs to a query. This is in two parts: a set of values known now, and a set of
types known now.
The separate map of types is to allow queries to be algebrized without full knowledge of
the bindings that will be used at execution time.
When built correctly, <code>types</code> is guaranteed to contain the types of <code>values</code> -- use
<code>QueryInputs::new</code> or <code>QueryInputs::with_values</code> to construct an instance.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>RelResult</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_query_projector/relresult.rs.html#35-38' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct RelResult&lt;T&gt; {
    pub width: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a>,
    pub values: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;T&gt;,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The result you get from a 'rel' query, like:</p>
<pre><code class="language-edn">[:find ?person ?name
 :where [?person :person/name ?name]]
</code></pre>
<p>There are three ways to get data out of a <code>RelResult</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li>By iterating over rows as slices. Use <code>result.rows()</code>. This is efficient and is
recommended in two cases:
<ol>
<li>If you don't need to take ownership of the resulting values (e.g., you're comparing
or making a modified clone).</li>
<li>When the data you're retrieving is cheap to clone. All scalar values are relatively
cheap: they're either small values or <code>Rc</code>.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>By direct reference to a row by index, using <code>result.row(i)</code>. This also returns
a reference.</li>
<li>By consuming the results using <code>into_iter</code>. This allocates short-lived vectors,
but gives you ownership of the enclosed <code>TypedValue</code>s.</li>
</ul>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>

maps.</p>

    pub tx_id: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>,
    pub tx_instant: <a class="struct" href="../mentat/struct.DateTime.html" title="struct mentat::DateTime">DateTime</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../mentat/struct.Utc.html" title="struct mentat::Utc">Utc</a>&gt;,

}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A transaction report summarizes an applied transaction.</p>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.tx_id" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.tx_id" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="tx_id.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>tx_id: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The transaction ID of the transaction.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.tx_instant" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.tx_instant" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="tx_instant.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>tx_instant: <a class="struct" href="../mentat/struct.DateTime.html" title="struct mentat::DateTime">DateTime</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../mentat/struct.Utc.html" title="struct mentat::Utc">Utc</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The timestamp when the transaction began to be committed.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.tempids" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.tempids" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="tempids.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>tempids: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>, <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A map from string literal tempid to resolved or allocated entid.</p>
<p>Every string literal tempid presented to the transactor either resolves via upsert to an
existing entid, or is allocated a new entid.  (It is possible for multiple distinct string
literal tempids to all unify to a single freshly allocated entid.)</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>Utc</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.0/src/chrono/offset/utc.rs.html#33' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct Utc;</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The UTC time zone. This is the most efficient time zone when you don't need the local time.
It is also used as an offset (which is also a dummy type).</p>
<p>Using the <a href="./trait.TimeZone.html"><code>TimeZone</code></a> methods
on the UTC struct is the preferred way to construct <code>DateTime&lt;Utc&gt;</code>
instances.</p>
<h1 id="example" class="section-header"><a href="#example">Example</a></h1>
<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">
<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">chrono</span>::{<span class="ident">DateTime</span>, <span class="ident">TimeZone</span>, <span class="ident">NaiveDateTime</span>, <span class="ident">Utc</span>};

<span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">dt</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">DateTime</span>::<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">Utc</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>::<span class="ident">from_utc</span>(<span class="ident">NaiveDateTime</span>::<span class="ident">from_timestamp</span>(<span class="number">61</span>, <span class="number">0</span>), <span class="ident">Utc</span>);

<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">Utc</span>.<span class="ident">timestamp</span>(<span class="number">61</span>, <span class="number">0</span>), <span class="ident">dt</span>);
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">Utc</span>.<span class="ident">ymd</span>(<span class="number">1970</span>, <span class="number">1</span>, <span class="number">1</span>).<span class="ident">and_hms</span>(<span class="number">0</span>, <span class="number">1</span>, <span class="number">1</span>), <span class="ident">dt</span>);</pre>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Type Definition <a href='index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a class="type" href=''>Entid</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#57' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><pre class='rust typedef'>type Entid = <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>;</pre><div class='docblock'><p>Represents one entid in the entid space.</p>
<p>Per https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html (see also http://stackoverflow.com/a/8499544), SQLite
stores signed integers up to 64 bits in size.  Since u32 is not appropriate for our use case, we
use i64 rather than manually truncating u64 to u63 and casting to i64 throughout the codebase.</p>
</div></section>

It prevents other
connections from taking immediate or exclusive transactions. This is appropriate for our
writes and <code>InProgress</code>: it means we are ready to write whenever we want to, and nobody else
can start a transaction that's not <code>DEFERRED</code>, but we don't need exclusivity yet.</p>

The attribute should be a namespaced string: e.g., <code>:foo/bar</code>.
<code>cache_action</code> determines if the attribute should be added or removed from the cache.
CacheAction::Add is idempotent - each attribute is only added once.
CacheAction::Remove throws an error if the attribute does not currently exist in the cache.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>conn</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>InProgress</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat/conn.rs.html#195-205' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct InProgress&lt;'a, 'c&gt; { /* fields omitted */ }</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Represents an in-progress, not yet committed, set of changes to the store.
Call <code>commit</code> to commit your changes, or <code>rollback</code> to discard them.
A transaction is held open until you do so.
Your changes will be implicitly dropped along with this struct.</p>
</div>
                    <h2 id='methods' class='small-section-header'>
                      Methods<a href='#methods' class='anchor'></a>

If the attribute is multi-valued, an arbitrary value is returned. If no value is present for that entity, `None` is returned. If `attribute` isn't an attribute, `None` is returned."],["lookup_value_for_attribute","Return a single value for the provided entity and attribute. If the attribute is multi-valued, an arbitrary value is returned. If no value is present for that entity, `None` is returned. If `attribute` doesn't name an attribute, an error is returned."],["lookup_values",""],["lookup_values_for_attribute",""],["q_explain",""],["q_once","Take an EDN query string, a reference to an open SQLite connection, a Mentat schema, and an optional collection of input bindings (which should be keyed by `\"?varname\"`), and execute the query immediately, blocking the current thread. Returns a structure that corresponds to the kind of input query, populated with `TypedValue` instances. The caller is responsible for ensuring that the SQLite connection has an open transaction if isolation is required."],["q_prepare",""],["q_uncached","Just like `q_once`, but doesn't use any cached values."]],"struct":[["Keyword","A keyword is a symbol, optionally with a namespace, that prints with a leading colon. This concept is imported from Clojure, as it features in EDN and the query syntax that we use."],["Known","A convenience wrapper around things known in memory: the schema and caches. We use a trait object here to avoid making dozens of functions generic over the type of the cache. If performance becomes a concern, we should hard-code specific kinds of cache right here, and/or eliminate the Option."],["PlainSymbol","A simplification of Clojure's Symbol."],["QueryInputs","Define the inputs to a query. This is in two parts: a set of values known now, and a set of types known now. The separate map of types is to allow queries to be algebrized without full knowledge of the bindings that will be used at execution time. When built correctly, `types` is guaranteed to contain the types of `values` -- use `QueryInputs::new` or `QueryInputs::with_values` to construct an instance."],["QueryOutput",""],["QueryPlanStep","A single row in the output of SQLite's `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`.                </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat_query_algebrizer/clauses/inputs.rs.html#33-36' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct QueryInputs { /* fields omitted */ }</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Define the inputs to a query. This is in two parts: a set of values known now, and a set of
types known now.
The separate map of types is to allow queries to be algebrized without full knowledge of
the bindings that will be used at execution time.
When built correctly, <code>types</code> is guaranteed to contain the types of <code>values</code> -- use
<code>QueryInputs::new</code> or <code>QueryInputs::with_values</code> to construct an instance.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>query</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>RelResult</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat_query_projector/relresult.rs.html#35-38' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct RelResult&lt;T&gt; {
    pub width: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a>,
    pub values: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;T&gt;,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The result you get from a 'rel' query, like:</p>
<pre><code class="language-edn">[:find ?person ?name
 :where [?person :person/name ?name]]
</code></pre>
<p>There are three ways to get data out of a <code>RelResult</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li>By iterating over rows as slices. Use <code>result.rows()</code>. This is efficient and is
recommended in two cases:
<ol>
<li>If you don't need to take ownership of the resulting values (e.g., you're comparing
or making a modified clone).</li>
<li>When the data you're retrieving is cheap to clone. All scalar values are relatively
cheap: they're either small values or <code>Rc</code>.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>By direct reference to a row by index, using <code>result.row(i)</code>. This also returns
a reference.</li>
<li>By consuming the results using <code>into_iter</code>. This allocates short-lived vectors,
but gives you ownership of the enclosed <code>TypedValue</code>s.</li>
</ul>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Module <a href='../index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a class="mod" href=''>vocabulary</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat/vocabulary.rs.html#12-960' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class='docblock'><p>This module exposes an interface for programmatic management of vocabularies.</p>
<p>A vocabulary is defined by a name, a version number, and a collection of attribute definitions.</p>
<p>Operations on vocabularies can include migrations between versions. These are defined
programmatically as a pair of functions, <code>pre</code> and <code>post</code>, that are invoked prior to
an upgrade.</p>
<p>A Mentat store exposes, via the <code>HasSchema</code> trait, operations to read
vocabularies by name or in bulk.</p>
<p>An in-progress transaction (<code>InProgress</code>) further exposes a trait,
<code>VersionedStore</code>, which allows for a vocabulary definition to be
checked for existence in the store, and transacted if needed.</p>
<p>Typical use is the following:</p>

<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">macro_use</span>(<span class="ident">kw</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">extern</span> <span class="kw">crate</span> <span class="ident">mentat</span>;

<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">mentat</span>::{
    <span class="ident">Store</span>,
    <span class="ident">ValueType</span>,
};

<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">mentat</span>::<span class="ident">vocabulary</span>;
<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">mentat</span>::<span class="ident">vocabulary</span>::{
    <span class="ident">Definition</span>,
    <span class="ident">HasVocabularies</span>,
    <span class="ident">VersionedStore</span>,
    <span class="ident">VocabularyOutcome</span>,
};

<span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">main</span>() {
    <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="kw-2">mut</span> <span class="ident">store</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">Store</span>::<span class="ident">open</span>(<span class="string">&quot;&quot;</span>).<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;connected&quot;</span>);

    {
        <span class="comment">// Read the list of installed vocabularies.</span>
        <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">reader</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">store</span>.<span class="ident">begin_read</span>().<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;began read&quot;</span>);
        <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">vocabularies</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">reader</span>.<span class="ident">read_vocabularies</span>().<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;read&quot;</span>);
        <span class="kw">for</span> (<span class="ident">name</span>, <span class="ident">vocabulary</span>) <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="ident">vocabularies</span>.<span class="ident">iter</span>() {
            <span class="macro">println</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;Vocab {} is at version {}.&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">name</span>, <span class="ident">vocabulary</span>.<span class="ident">version</span>);
            <span class="kw">for</span> <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span>(<span class="kw-2">ref</span> <span class="ident">name</span>, <span class="kw-2">ref</span> <span class="ident">attr</span>) <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="ident">vocabulary</span>.<span class="ident">attributes</span>().<span class="ident">iter</span>() {
                <span class="macro">println</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;  &gt;&gt; {} ({})&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">name</span>, <span class="ident">attr</span>.<span class="ident">value_type</span>);
            }
        }
    }

    {
        <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="kw-2">mut</span> <span class="ident">in_progress</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">store</span>.<span class="ident">begin_transaction</span>().<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;began transaction&quot;</span>);

        <span class="comment">// Make sure the core vocabulary exists.</span>
        <span class="ident">in_progress</span>.<span class="ident">verify_core_schema</span>().<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;verified&quot;</span>);

        <span class="comment">// Make sure our vocabulary is installed, and install if necessary.</span>
        <span class="ident">in_progress</span>.<span class="ident">ensure_vocabulary</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">Definition</span> {
            <span class="ident">name</span>: <span class="macro">kw</span><span class="macro">!</span>(:<span class="ident">example</span><span class="op">/</span><span class="ident">links</span>),
            <span class="ident">version</span>: <span class="number">1</span>,
            <span class="ident">attributes</span>: <span class="macro">vec</span><span class="macro">!</span>[
                (<span class="macro">kw</span><span class="macro">!</span>(:<span class="ident">link</span><span class="op">/</span><span class="ident">title</span>),
                 <span class="ident">vocabulary</span>::<span class="ident">AttributeBuilder</span>::<span class="ident">helpful</span>()
                   .<span class="ident">value_type</span>(<span class="ident">ValueType</span>::<span class="ident">String</span>)
                   .<span class="ident">multival</span>(<span class="bool-val">false</span>)
                   .<span class="ident">fulltext</span>(<span class="bool-val">true</span>)
                   .<span class="ident">build</span>()),
            ],
            <span class="ident">pre</span>: <span class="ident">Definition</span>::<span class="ident">no_op</span>,
            <span class="ident">post</span>: <span class="ident">Definition</span>::<span class="ident">no_op</span>,
        }).<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;ensured&quot;</span>);

        <span class="comment">// Now we can do stuff.</span>
        <span class="ident">in_progress</span>.<span class="ident">transact</span>(<span class="string">&quot;[{:link/title \&quot;Title\&quot;}]&quot;</span>).<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;transacts&quot;</span>);
        <span class="ident">in_progress</span>.<span class="ident">commit</span>().<span class="ident">expect</span>(<span class="string">&quot;commits&quot;</span>);
    }
}</pre>
<p>A similar approach is taken using the
<a href="mentat::vocabulary::VocabularyProvider">VocabularyProvider</a> trait to handle migrations across
multiple vocabularies.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../index.html'>mentat</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>vocabulary</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>Definition</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]

               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat/vocabulary.rs.html#159-165' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct Definition {
    pub name: <a class="struct" href="../../mentat/query/struct.Keyword.html" title="struct mentat::query::Keyword">Keyword</a>,
    pub version: <a class="type" href="../../mentat/vocabulary/type.Version.html" title="type mentat::vocabulary::Version">Version</a>,
    pub attributes: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">(</a><a class="struct" href="../../mentat/query/struct.Keyword.html" title="struct mentat::query::Keyword">Keyword</a>, <a class="struct" href="../../mentat/struct.Attribute.html" title="struct mentat::Attribute">Attribute</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">)</a>&gt;,
    pub pre: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.fn.html">fn</a>(_: &amp;mut <a class="struct" href="../../mentat/conn/struct.InProgress.html" title="struct mentat::conn::InProgress">InProgress</a>, _: &amp;<a class="struct" href="../../mentat/vocabulary/struct.Vocabulary.html" title="struct mentat::vocabulary::Vocabulary">Vocabulary</a>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html">()</a>&gt;,
    pub post: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.fn.html">fn</a>(_: &amp;mut <a class="struct" href="../../mentat/conn/struct.InProgress.html" title="struct mentat::conn::InProgress">InProgress</a>, _: &amp;<a class="struct" href="../../mentat/vocabulary/struct.Vocabulary.html" title="struct mentat::vocabulary::Vocabulary">Vocabulary</a>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html">()</a>&gt;,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A definition of an attribute that is independent of a particular store.</p>
<p><code>Attribute</code> instances not only aren't named, but don't even have entids.</p>
<p>We need two kinds of structure: an abstract definition of a vocabulary in terms of names,
and a concrete instance of a vocabulary in a particular store.</p>
<p><code>Definition</code> is the former, and <code>Vocabulary</code> is the latter.</p>
<p>Note that, because it's possible to 'flesh out' a vocabulary with attributes without bumping
its version number, we need to track the attributes that the application cares about — it's
not enough to know the name and version. Indeed, we even care about the details of each attribute,
because that's how we'll detect errors.</p>
<p><code>Definition</code> includes two additional fields: functions to run if this vocabulary is being
upgraded. <code>pre</code> and <code>post</code> are run before and after the definition is transacted against the
store. Each is called with the existing <code>Vocabulary</code> instance so that they can do version
checks or employ more fine-grained logic.</p>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='index.html'>mentat_core</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>AttributeBitFlags</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>

    IndexAVET,
    IndexVAET,
    IndexFulltext,
    UniqueValue,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Bit flags used in <code>flags0</code> column in temporary tables created during search,
such as the <code>search_results</code>, <code>inexact_searches</code> and <code>exact_searches</code> tables.
When moving to a more concrete table, such as <code>datoms</code>, they are expanded out
via these flags and put into their own column rather than a bit field.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='index.html'>mentat_core</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>Binding</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#231-235' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum Binding {
    Scalar(<a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/enum.TypedValue.html" title="enum mentat_core::TypedValue">TypedValue</a>),
    Vec(<a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.ValueRc.html" title="type mentat_core::ValueRc">ValueRc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/enum.Binding.html" title="enum mentat_core::Binding">Binding</a>&gt;&gt;),
    Map(<a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.ValueRc.html" title="type mentat_core::ValueRc">ValueRc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../mentat_core/struct.StructuredMap.html" title="struct mentat_core::StructuredMap">StructuredMap</a>&gt;),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The values bound in a query specification can be:</p>
<ul>
<li>Vecs of structured values, for multi-valued component attributes or nested expressions.</li>
<li>Single structured values, for single-valued component attributes or nested expressions.</li>
<li>Single typed values, for simple attributes.</li>
</ul>
<p>The <code>Binding</code> enum defines these three options.</p>
<p>Datomic also supports structured inputs; at present Mentat does not, but this type
would also serve that purpose.</p>
<p>Note that maps are not ordered, and so <code>Binding</code> is neither <code>Ord</code> nor <code>PartialOrd</code>.</p>

</div>pub enum ValueType {
    Ref,
    Boolean,
    Instant,
    Long,
    Double,
    String,
    Keyword,
    Uuid,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The attribute of each Mentat assertion has a :db/valueType constraining the value to a
particular set.  Mentat recognizes the following :db/valueType values.</p>

For
example, <code>1</code> is how we encode <code>true</code>.</p>

<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">
<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">mentat_core</span>::{<span class="ident">ValueType</span>, <span class="ident">SQLValueType</span>};
<span class="macro">assert</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="op">!</span><span class="ident">ValueType</span>::<span class="ident">Instant</span>.<span class="ident">accommodates_integer</span>(<span class="number">1493399581314</span>));

                                <p>We have an enum of types, <code>ValueType</code>. It can be collected into a set, <code>ValueTypeSet</code>. Each type
is associated with a type tag, which is how a type is represented in, e.g., SQL storage. Types
can share type tags, because backing SQL storage is able to differentiate between some types
(e.g., longs and doubles), and so distinct tags aren't necessary. That association is defined by
<code>SQLValueType</code>. That trait similarly extends to <code>ValueTypeSet</code>, which maps a collection of types
into a collection of tags.</p>

    pub value_type: <a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/enum.ValueType.html" title="enum mentat_core::ValueType">ValueType</a>,
