}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A Mentat schema attribute has a value type and several other flags determining how assertions
with the attribute are interpreted.</p>
<p>TODO: consider packing this into a bitfield or similar.</p>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.value_type" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.value_type" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="value_type.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>value_type: <a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/enum.ValueType.html" title="enum mentat_core::ValueType">ValueType</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The associated value type, i.e., <code>:db/valueType</code>?</p>
</div><span id="structfield.multival" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.multival" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="multival.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>multival: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is multi-valued, i.e., it is <code>:db/cardinality :db.cardinality/many</code>.  <code>false</code> if this attribute is single-valued (the default), i.e., it
is <code>:db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.unique" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.unique" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="unique.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>unique: <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/attribute/enum.Unique.html" title="enum mentat_core::attribute::Unique">Unique</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>None</code> if this attribute is neither unique-value nor unique-identity.</p>
<p><code>Some(attribute::Unique::Value)</code> if this attribute is unique-value, i.e., it is <code>:db/unique :db.unique/value</code>.</p>
<p><em>Unique-value</em> means that there is at most one assertion with the attribute and a
particular value in the datom store.  Unique-value attributes can be used in lookup-refs.</p>
<p><code>Some(attribute::Unique::Identity)</code> if this attribute is unique-identity, i.e., it is <code>:db/unique :db.unique/identity</code>.</p>
<p>Unique-identity attributes always have value type <code>Ref</code>.</p>
<p><em>Unique-identity</em> means that the attribute is <em>unique-value</em> and that they can be used in
lookup-refs and will automatically upsert where appropriate.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.index" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.index" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="index.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>index: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is automatically indexed, i.e., it is <code>:db/indexing true</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.fulltext" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.fulltext" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="fulltext.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>fulltext: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is automatically fulltext indexed, i.e., it is <code>:db/fulltext true</code>.</p>
<p>Fulltext attributes always have string values.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.component" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.component" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="component.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>component: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is a component, i.e., it is <code>:db/isComponent true</code>.</p>
<p>Component attributes always have value type <code>Ref</code>.</p>
<p>They are used to compose entities from component sub-entities: they are fetched recursively
by pull expressions, and they are automatically recursively deleted where appropriate.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.no_history" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.no_history" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="no_history.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>no_history: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute doesn't require history to be kept, i.e., it is <code>:db/noHistory true</code>.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat_core</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>Schema</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/lib.rs.html#257-277' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct Schema {
    pub entid_map: <a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.EntidMap.html" title="type mentat_core::EntidMap">EntidMap</a>,
    pub ident_map: <a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.IdentMap.html" title="type mentat_core::IdentMap">IdentMap</a>,
    pub attribute_map: <a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.AttributeMap.html" title="type mentat_core::AttributeMap">AttributeMap</a>,
    pub component_attributes: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_core::Entid">Entid</a>&gt;,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Represents a Mentat schema.</p>
<p>Maintains the mapping between string idents and positive integer entids; and exposes the schema
flags associated to a given entid (equivalently, ident).</p>
<p>TODO: consider a single bi-directional map instead of separate ident-&gt;entid and entid-&gt;ident
maps.</p>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.entid_map" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.entid_map" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="entid_map.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>entid_map: <a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.EntidMap.html" title="type mentat_core::EntidMap">EntidMap</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Map entid-&gt;ident.</p>
<p>Invariant: is the inverse map of <code>ident_map</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.ident_map" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.ident_map" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="ident_map.v" class='invisible'>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Map ident-&gt;entid.</p>
<p>Invariant: is the inverse map of <code>entid_map</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.attribute_map" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.attribute_map" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="attribute_map.v" class='invisible'>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Map entid-&gt;attribute flags.</p>
<p>Invariant: key-set is the same as the key-set of <code>entid_map</code> (equivalently, the value-set of
<code>ident_map</code>).</p>
</div><span id="structfield.component_attributes" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.component_attributes" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="component_attributes.v" class='invisible'>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Maintain a vec of unique attribute IDs for which the corresponding attribute in <code>attribute_map</code>
has <code>.component == true</code>.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat_core</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>StructuredMap</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#275' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct StructuredMap(pub <a class="struct" href="https://docs.rs/indexmap/1/indexmap/map/struct.IndexMap.html" title="struct indexmap::map::IndexMap">IndexMap</a>&lt;<a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.ValueRc.html" title="type mentat_core::ValueRc">ValueRc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../mentat_core/struct.Keyword.html" title="struct mentat_core::Keyword">Keyword</a>&gt;, <a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/enum.Binding.html" title="enum mentat_core::Binding">Binding</a>&gt;);</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A pull expression expands a binding into a structure. The returned structure
associates attributes named in the input or retrieved from the store with values.
This association is a <code>StructuredMap</code>.</p>
<p>Note that 'attributes' in Datomic's case can mean:</p>
<ul>
<li>Reversed attribute keywords (:artist/_country).</li>
<li>An alias using <code>:as</code> (:artist/name :as &quot;Band name&quot;).</li>
</ul>
<p>We entirely support the former, and partially support the latter -- you can alias
using a different keyword only.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat_core</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>Utc</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.0/src/chrono/offset/utc.rs.html#33' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct Utc;</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The UTC time zone. This is the most efficient time zone when you don't need the local time.
It is also used as an offset (which is also a dummy type).</p>
<p>Using the <a href="./trait.TimeZone.html"><code>TimeZone</code></a> methods
on the UTC struct is the preferred way to construct <code>DateTime&lt;Utc&gt;</code>
instances.</p>
<h1 id="example" class="section-header"><a href="#example">Example</a></h1>
<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">
<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">chrono</span>::{<span class="ident">DateTime</span>, <span class="ident">TimeZone</span>, <span class="ident">NaiveDateTime</span>, <span class="ident">Utc</span>};

<span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">dt</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">DateTime</span>::<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">Utc</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>::<span class="ident">from_utc</span>(<span class="ident">NaiveDateTime</span>::<span class="ident">from_timestamp</span>(<span class="number">61</span>, <span class="number">0</span>), <span class="ident">Utc</span>);

<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">Utc</span>.<span class="ident">timestamp</span>(<span class="number">61</span>, <span class="number">0</span>), <span class="ident">dt</span>);
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">Utc</span>.<span class="ident">ymd</span>(<span class="number">1970</span>, <span class="number">1</span>, <span class="number">1</span>).<span class="ident">and_hms</span>(<span class="number">0</span>, <span class="number">1</span>, <span class="number">1</span>), <span class="ident">dt</span>);</pre>

<div class='docblock'><p>The type of the elements being iterated over.</p>

                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.

        <h3 id='tymethod.value_type_tag' class='method'><span id='value_type_tag.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.value_type_tag' class='fnname'>value_type_tag</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.ValueTypeTag.html" title="type mentat_core::ValueTypeTag">ValueTypeTag</a></code></span></h3><h3 id='tymethod.accommodates_integer' class='method'><span id='accommodates_integer.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.accommodates_integer' class='fnname'>accommodates_integer</a>(&amp;self, int: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></h3><h3 id='tymethod.sql_representation' class='method'><span id='sql_representation.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.sql_representation' class='fnname'>sql_representation</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">(</a><a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.ValueTypeTag.html" title="type mentat_core::ValueTypeTag">ValueTypeTag</a>, <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/enum.SQLTypeAffinity.html" title="enum mentat_core::SQLTypeAffinity">SQLTypeAffinity</a>&gt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">)</a></code></span></h3><div class='docblock'><p>Return a pair of the ValueTypeTag for this value type, and the SQLTypeAffinity required
to distinguish it from any other types that share the same tag.</p>
<p>Background: The tag alone is not enough to determine the type of a value, since multiple
ValueTypes may share the same tag (for example, ValueType::Long and ValueType::Double).
However, each ValueType can be determined by checking both the tag and the type's affinity.</p>

    fn <a href='#tymethod.value_type_tags' class='fnname'>value_type_tags</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/set/struct.BTreeSet.html" title="struct alloc::btree::set::BTreeSet">BTreeSet</a>&lt;<a class="type" href="../mentat_core/type.ValueTypeTag.html" title="type mentat_core::ValueTypeTag">ValueTypeTag</a>&gt;;
<div class='item-spacer'></div>    fn <a href='#tymethod.has_unique_type_tag' class='fnname'>has_unique_type_tag</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a>;

}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>We have an enum of types, <code>ValueType</code>. It can be collected into a set, <code>ValueTypeSet</code>. Each type
is associated with a type tag, which is how a type is represented in, e.g., SQL storage. Types
can share type tags, because backing SQL storage is able to differentiate between some types
(e.g., longs and doubles), and so distinct tags aren't necessary. That association is defined by
<code>SQLValueType</code>. That trait similarly extends to <code>ValueTypeSet</code>, which maps a collection of types
into a collection of tags.</p>
</div>

                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#57' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><pre class='rust typedef'>type Entid = <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>;</pre><div class='docblock'><p>Represents one entid in the entid space.</p>
<p>Per https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html (see also http://stackoverflow.com/a/8499544), SQLite
stores signed integers up to 64 bits in size.  Since u32 is not appropriate for our use case, we
use i64 rather than manually truncating u64 to u63 and casting to i64 throughout the codebase.</p>
</div>

}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>An <code>InternSet</code> allows to &quot;intern&quot; some potentially large values, maintaining a single value
instance owned by the <code>InternSet</code> and leaving consumers with lightweight ref-counted handles to
the large owned value.  This can avoid expensive clone() operations.</p>
<p>In Mentat, such large values might be strings or arbitrary [a v] pairs.</p>
<p>See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_interning for discussion.</p>

the provided <code>a</code>, if <code>a</code> names an attribute that is
cached in the forward direction. If <code>a</code> doesn't name an attribute, or it's not cached at
all, or it's only cached in reverse (<code>v</code> to <code>e</code>, not <code>e</code> to <code>v</code>), <code>None</code> is returned.</p>

The caller is responsible for ensuring that <code>entities</code> is unique.
Attributes for which every entity is already cached will not be processed again.</p>

            <div class="infos">
                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>

}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p><code>MentatStoring</code> will be the trait that encapsulates the storage layer.  It is consumed by the
transaction processing layer.</p>
<p>Right now, the only implementation of <code>MentatStoring</code> is the SQLite-specific SQL schema.  In the
future, we might consider other SQL engines (perhaps with different fulltext indexing), or
entirely different data stores, say ones shaped like key-value stores.</p>
</div>
            <h2 id='required-methods' class='small-section-header'>
              Required Methods<a href='#required-methods' class='anchor'></a>
            </h2>
            <div class='methods'>
        <h3 id='tymethod.resolve_avs' class='method'><span id='resolve_avs.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.resolve_avs' class='fnname'>resolve_avs</a>&lt;'a&gt;(&amp;self, avs: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html">&amp;'a [</a>&amp;'a <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.AVPair.html" title="type mentat_db::types::AVPair">AVPair</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html">]</a>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat_db::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.AVMap.html" title="type mentat_db::types::AVMap">AVMap</a>&lt;'a&gt;&gt;</code></span></h3><div class='docblock'><p>Given a slice of [a v] lookup-refs, look up the corresponding [e a v] triples.</p>
<p>It is assumed that the attribute <code>a</code> in each lookup-ref is <code>:db/unique</code>, so that at most one
matching [e a v] triple exists.  (If this is not true, some matching entid <code>e</code> will be
chosen non-deterministically, if one exists.)</p>
<p>Returns a map &amp;(a, v) -&gt; e, to avoid cloning potentially large values.  The keys of the map
are exactly those (a, v) pairs that have an assertion [e a v] in the store.</p>
</div><h3 id='tymethod.begin_tx_application' class='method'><span id='begin_tx_application.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.begin_tx_application' class='fnname'>begin_tx_application</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat_db::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html">()</a>&gt;</code></span></h3><div class='docblock'><p>Begin (or prepare) the underlying storage layer for a new Mentat transaction.</p>
<p>Use this to create temporary tables, prepare indices, set pragmas, etc, before the initial
<code>insert_non_fts_searches</code> invocation.</p>
</div><h3 id='tymethod.insert_non_fts_searches' class='method'><span id='insert_non_fts_searches.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.insert_non_fts_searches' class='fnname'>insert_non_fts_searches</a>&lt;'a&gt;(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&amp;self, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;entities: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html">&amp;'a [</a><a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/db/type.ReducedEntity.html" title="type mentat_db::db::ReducedEntity">ReducedEntity</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html">]</a>, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;search_type: <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/db/enum.SearchType.html" title="enum mentat_db::db::SearchType">SearchType</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat_db::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html">()</a>&gt;</code></span></h3><h3 id='tymethod.insert_fts_searches' class='method'><span id='insert_fts_searches.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.insert_fts_searches' class='fnname'>insert_fts_searches</a>&lt;'a&gt;(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&amp;self, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;entities: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html">&amp;'a [</a><a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/db/type.ReducedEntity.html" title="type mentat_db::db::ReducedEntity">ReducedEntity</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html">]</a>, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;search_type: <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/db/enum.SearchType.html" title="enum mentat_db::db::SearchType">SearchType</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat_db::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html">()</a>&gt;</code></span></h3><h3 id='tymethod.commit_transaction' class='method'><span id='commit_transaction.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.commit_transaction' class='fnname'>commit_transaction</a>(&amp;self, tx_id: <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat_db::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html">()</a>&gt;</code></span></h3><div class='docblock'><p>Finalize the underlying storage layer after a Mentat transaction.</p>
<p>Use this to finalize temporary tables, complete indices, revert pragmas, etc, after the
final <code>insert_non_fts_searches</code> invocation.</p>
</div><h3 id='tymethod.committed_metadata_assertions' class='method'><span id='committed_metadata_assertions.v' class='invisible'><code>fn <a href='#tymethod.committed_metadata_assertions' class='fnname'>committed_metadata_assertions</a>(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&amp;self, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;tx_id: <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat_db::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">(</a><a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a>, <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a>, <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/types/enum.TypedValue.html" title="enum mentat_db::types::TypedValue">TypedValue</a>, <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">)</a>&gt;&gt;</code></span></h3><div class='docblock'><p>Extract metadata-related [e a typed_value added] datoms committed in the given transaction.</p>

        conflicting_datoms: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">(</a><a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a>, <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a>, <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/types/enum.TypedValue.html" title="enum mentat_db::types::TypedValue">TypedValue</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">)</a>, <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/types/enum.ValueType.html" title="enum mentat_db::types::ValueType">ValueType</a>&gt;,
    },
    CardinalityConflicts {
        conflicts: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/errors/enum.CardinalityConflict.html" title="enum mentat_db::errors::CardinalityConflict">CardinalityConflict</a>&gt;,
    },
}</pre></div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>
                   Variants<a href='#variants' class='anchor'></a></h2>
<span id="variant.ConflictingUpserts" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.ConflictingUpserts" class="anchor field"></a><span id='ConflictingUpserts.v' class='invisible'><code>ConflictingUpserts</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A transaction tried to assert datoms where one tempid upserts to two (or more) distinct
entids.</p>
</div><span class='docblock autohide sub-variant' id='variant.ConflictingUpserts.fields'><h3 class='fields'>Fields of <code>ConflictingUpserts</code></h3>

                           <table><tr><td id='variant.ConflictingUpserts.field.conflicting_upserts'><span id='ConflictingUpserts.v.conflicting_upserts.v' class='invisible'><code>conflicting_upserts:&nbsp;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../edn/entities/enum.TempId.html" title="enum edn::entities::TempId">TempId</a>, <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/set/struct.BTreeSet.html" title="struct alloc::btree::set::BTreeSet">BTreeSet</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../../mentat_core/types/struct.KnownEntid.html" title="struct mentat_core::types::KnownEntid">KnownEntid</a>&gt;&gt;</code></span></td><td><div class='docblock'><p>A map from tempid to the entids it would upsert to.</p>
<p>In the future, we might even be able to attribute the upserts to particular (reduced)
datoms, i.e., to particular <code>[e a v]</code> triples that caused the constraint violation.
Attributing constraint violations to input data is more difficult to the multiple
rewriting passes the input undergoes.</p>
</div></td></tr></table></span><span id="variant.TypeDisagreements" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.TypeDisagreements" class="anchor field"></a><span id='TypeDisagreements.v' class='invisible'><code>TypeDisagreements</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A transaction tried to assert a datom or datoms with the wrong value <code>v</code> type(s).</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='../index.html'>mentat_db</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>internal_types</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>LookupRefOrTempId</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>

    LookupRef(<a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/internal_types/type.LookupRef.html" title="type mentat_db::internal_types::LookupRef">LookupRef</a>),
    TempId(<a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/internal_types/type.TempIdHandle.html" title="type mentat_db::internal_types::TempIdHandle">TempIdHandle</a>),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Internal representation of an entid on its way to resolution.  We either have the simple case (a
numeric entid), a lookup-ref that still needs to be resolved (an atomized [a v] pair), or a temp
ID that needs to be upserted or allocated (an atomized tempid).</p>
</div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>
                   Variants<a href='#variants' class='anchor'></a></h2>

            <div class="infos">
                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Accepted types are: <code>fn</code>, <code>mod</code>,

                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat_db/internal_types.rs.html#193-206' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><pre class='rust fn'>pub fn replace_lookup_ref&lt;T, U&gt;(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;lookup_map: &amp;<a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.AVMap.html" title="type mentat_db::types::AVMap">AVMap</a>, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;desired_or: <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_core/util/enum.Either.html" title="enum mentat_core::util::Either">Either</a>&lt;T, <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/internal_types/enum.LookupRefOrTempId.html" title="enum mentat_db::internal_types::LookupRefOrTempId">LookupRefOrTempId</a>&gt;, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;lift: U<br>) -&gt; <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/errors/type.Result.html" title="type mentat_db::errors::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../mentat_core/util/enum.Either.html" title="enum mentat_core::util::Either">Either</a>&lt;T, <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/internal_types/type.TempIdHandle.html" title="type mentat_db::internal_types::TempIdHandle">TempIdHandle</a>&gt;&gt; <span class="where fmt-newline">where<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;U: <a class="trait" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(<a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a>) -&gt; T,&nbsp;</span></pre><div class='docblock'><p>Given a <code>KnownEntidOr</code> or a <code>TypedValueOr</code>, replace any internal <code>LookupRef</code> with the entid from
the given map.  Fail if any <code>LookupRef</code> cannot be replaced.</p>
<p><code>lift</code> allows to specify how the entid found is mapped into the output type.  (This could
also be an <code>Into</code> or <code>From</code> requirement.)</p>
<p>The reason for this awkward expression is that we're parameterizing over the <em>type constructor</em>
(<code>EntidOr</code> or <code>TypedValueOr</code>), which is not trivial to express in Rust.  This only works because
they're both the same <code>Result&lt;...&gt;</code> type with different parameterizations.</p>
</div></section>

such as the <code>search_results</code>, <code>inexact_searches</code> and <code>exact_searches</code> tables.

via these flags and put into their own column rather than a bit field.</p>

with the attribute are interpreted.</p>
<p>TODO: consider packing this into a bitfield or similar.</p>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.value_type" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.value_type" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="value_type.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>value_type: <a class="enum" href="../../mentat_db/types/enum.ValueType.html" title="enum mentat_db::types::ValueType">ValueType</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The associated value type, i.e., <code>:db/valueType</code>?</p>
</div><span id="structfield.multival" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.multival" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="multival.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>multival: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is multi-valued, i.e., it is <code>:db/cardinality :db.cardinality/many</code>.  <code>false</code> if this attribute is single-valued (the default), i.e., it
is <code>:db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.unique" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.unique" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="unique.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>unique: <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../../mentat_core/attribute/enum.Unique.html" title="enum mentat_core::attribute::Unique">Unique</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>None</code> if this attribute is neither unique-value nor unique-identity.</p>
<p><code>Some(attribute::Unique::Value)</code> if this attribute is unique-value, i.e., it is <code>:db/unique :db.unique/value</code>.</p>
<p><em>Unique-value</em> means that there is at most one assertion with the attribute and a
particular value in the datom store.  Unique-value attributes can be used in lookup-refs.</p>
<p><code>Some(attribute::Unique::Identity)</code> if this attribute is unique-identity, i.e., it is <code>:db/unique :db.unique/identity</code>.</p>
<p>Unique-identity attributes always have value type <code>Ref</code>.</p>
<p><em>Unique-identity</em> means that the attribute is <em>unique-value</em> and that they can be used in
lookup-refs and will automatically upsert where appropriate.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.index" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.index" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="index.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>index: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is automatically indexed, i.e., it is <code>:db/indexing true</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.fulltext" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.fulltext" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="fulltext.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>fulltext: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is automatically fulltext indexed, i.e., it is <code>:db/fulltext true</code>.</p>
<p>Fulltext attributes always have string values.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.component" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.component" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="component.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>component: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute is a component, i.e., it is <code>:db/isComponent true</code>.</p>
<p>Component attributes always have value type <code>Ref</code>.</p>
<p>They are used to compose entities from component sub-entities: they are fetched recursively
by pull expressions, and they are automatically recursively deleted where appropriate.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.no_history" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.no_history" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="no_history.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>no_history: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>true</code> if this attribute doesn't require history to be kept, i.e., it is <code>:db/noHistory true</code>.</p>
</div>

<p>Maintains the mapping between string idents and positive integer entids; and exposes the schema
flags associated to a given entid (equivalently, ident).</p>
<p>TODO: consider a single bi-directional map instead of separate ident-&gt;entid and entid-&gt;ident
maps.</p>

                           <a href="#structfield.attribute_map" class="anchor field"></a>

                           <code>attribute_map: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>, <a class="struct" href="../../mentat_db/types/struct.Attribute.html" title="struct mentat_db::types::Attribute">Attribute</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Map entid-&gt;attribute flags.</p>
<p>Invariant: key-set is the same as the key-set of <code>entid_map</code> (equivalently, the value-set of
<code>ident_map</code>).</p>
</div><span id="structfield.component_attributes" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.component_attributes" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="component_attributes.v" class='invisible'>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Maintain a vec of unique attribute IDs for which the corresponding attribute in <code>attribute_map</code>
has <code>.component == true</code>.</p>

                           <code>tempids: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>, <a class="type" href="../../mentat_db/types/type.Entid.html" title="type mentat_db::types::Entid">Entid</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A map from string literal tempid to resolved or allocated entid.</p>
<p>Every string literal tempid presented to the transactor either resolves via upsert to an
existing entid, or is allocated a new entid.  (It is possible for multiple distinct string
literal tempids to all unify to a single freshly allocated entid.)</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../index.html'>mentat_db</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>types</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>Utc</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.0/src/chrono/offset/utc.rs.html#33' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct Utc;</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The UTC time zone. This is the most efficient time zone when you don't need the local time.
It is also used as an offset (which is also a dummy type).</p>
<p>Using the <a href="./trait.TimeZone.html"><code>TimeZone</code></a> methods
on the UTC struct is the preferred way to construct <code>DateTime&lt;Utc&gt;</code>
instances.</p>
<h1 id="example" class="section-header"><a href="#example">Example</a></h1>
<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">
<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">chrono</span>::{<span class="ident">DateTime</span>, <span class="ident">TimeZone</span>, <span class="ident">NaiveDateTime</span>, <span class="ident">Utc</span>};

<span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">dt</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">DateTime</span>::<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">Utc</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>::<span class="ident">from_utc</span>(<span class="ident">NaiveDateTime</span>::<span class="ident">from_timestamp</span>(<span class="number">61</span>, <span class="number">0</span>), <span class="ident">Utc</span>);

<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">Utc</span>.<span class="ident">timestamp</span>(<span class="number">61</span>, <span class="number">0</span>), <span class="ident">dt</span>);
<span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">Utc</span>.<span class="ident">ymd</span>(<span class="number">1970</span>, <span class="number">1</span>, <span class="number">1</span>).<span class="ident">and_hms</span>(<span class="number">0</span>, <span class="number">1</span>, <span class="number">1</span>), <span class="ident">dt</span>);</pre>
</div>

                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#57' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><pre class='rust typedef'>type Entid = <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>;</pre><div class='docblock'><p>Represents one entid in the entid space.</p>
<p>Per https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html (see also http://stackoverflow.com/a/8499544), SQLite
stores signed integers up to 64 bits in size.  Since u32 is not appropriate for our use case, we
use i64 rather than manually truncating u64 to u63 and casting to i64 throughout the codebase.</p>
</div></section>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='index.html'>mentat_ffi</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>Binding</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#231-235' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum Binding {
    Scalar(<a class="enum" href="../mentat_ffi/enum.TypedValue.html" title="enum mentat_ffi::TypedValue">TypedValue</a>),
    Vec(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/arc/struct.Arc.html" title="struct alloc::arc::Arc">Arc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_ffi/enum.Binding.html" title="enum mentat_ffi::Binding">Binding</a>&gt;&gt;),
    Map(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/arc/struct.Arc.html" title="struct alloc::arc::Arc">Arc</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../mentat_core/types/struct.StructuredMap.html" title="struct mentat_core::types::StructuredMap">StructuredMap</a>&gt;),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The values bound in a query specification can be:</p>
<ul>
<li>Vecs of structured values, for multi-valued component attributes or nested expressions.</li>
<li>Single structured values, for single-valued component attributes or nested expressions.</li>
<li>Single typed values, for simple attributes.</li>
</ul>
<p>The <code>Binding</code> enum defines these three options.</p>
<p>Datomic also supports structured inputs; at present Mentat does not, but this type
would also serve that purpose.</p>
<p>Note that maps are not ordered, and so <code>Binding</code> is neither <code>Ord</code> nor <code>PartialOrd</code>.</p>
</div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='index.html'>mentat_ffi</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>FindSpec</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#654-670' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum FindSpec {
    FindRel(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;),
    FindColl(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>),
    FindTuple(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;),
    FindScalar(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A definition of the first part of a find query: the
<code>[:find ?foo ?bar…]</code> bit.</p>
<p>There are four different kinds of find specs, allowing you to query for
a single value, a collection of values from different entities, a single
tuple (relation), or a collection of tuples.</p>
<p>Examples:</p>

<pre class="rust rust-example-rendered">


  <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">elements</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="macro">vec</span><span class="macro">!</span>[
    <span class="ident">Element</span>::<span class="ident">Variable</span>(<span class="ident">Variable</span>::<span class="ident">from_valid_name</span>(<span class="string">&quot;?foo&quot;</span>)),
    <span class="ident">Element</span>::<span class="ident">Variable</span>(<span class="ident">Variable</span>::<span class="ident">from_valid_name</span>(<span class="string">&quot;?bar&quot;</span>)),
  ];
  <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">rel</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">FindSpec</span>::<span class="ident">FindRel</span>(<span class="ident">elements</span>);

  <span class="kw">if</span> <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">FindSpec</span>::<span class="ident">FindRel</span>(<span class="ident">elements</span>) <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">rel</span> {
    <span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="number">2</span>, <span class="ident">elements</span>.<span class="ident">len</span>());
  }
</pre>
</div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>
                   Variants<a href='#variants' class='anchor'></a></h2>
<span id="variant.FindRel" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindRel" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindRel.v' class='invisible'><code>FindRel(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns an array of arrays, represented as a single array with length a multiple of width.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindColl" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindColl" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindColl.v' class='invisible'><code>FindColl(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns an array of scalars, usually homogeneous.
This is equivalent to mapping over the results of a <code>FindRel</code>,
returning the first value of each.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindTuple" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindTuple" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindTuple.v' class='invisible'><code>FindTuple(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns a single tuple: a heterogeneous array of scalars. Equivalent to
taking the first result from a <code>FindRel</code>.</p>
</div><span id="variant.FindScalar" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.FindScalar" class="anchor field"></a><span id='FindScalar.v' class='invisible'><code>FindScalar(<a class="enum" href="../edn/query/enum.Element.html" title="enum edn::query::Element">Element</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Returns a single scalar value. Equivalent to taking the first result
from a <code>FindColl</code>.</p>
</div>
                    <h2 id='methods' class='small-section-header'>
                      Methods<a href='#methods' class='anchor'></a>
                    </h2>
                <h3 id='impl' class='impl'><span class='in-band'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>impl <a class="enum" href="../mentat_ffi/enum.FindSpec.html" title="enum mentat_ffi::FindSpec">FindSpec</a></code><a href='#impl' class='anchor'></a></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#673-725' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></td></tr></tbody></table></h3><div class='docblock'><p>Returns true if the provided <code>FindSpec</code> returns at most one result.</p>
</div><div class='impl-items'><h4 id='method.is_unit_limited' class="method"><span id='is_unit_limited.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.is_unit_limited' class='fnname'>is_unit_limited</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#674-682' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><h4 id='method.expected_column_count' class="method"><span id='expected_column_count.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.expected_column_count' class='fnname'>expected_column_count</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#684-691' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><h4 id='method.requires_distinct' class="method"><span id='requires_distinct.v' class='invisible'><table class='table-display'><tbody><tr><td><code>pub fn <a href='#method.requires_distinct' class='fnname'>requires_distinct</a>(&amp;self) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code></span></td><td><span class='out-of-band'><div class='ghost'></div><a class='srclink' href='../src/edn/query.rs.html#712-714' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></td></tr></tbody></table></span></h4><div class='docblock'><p>Returns true if the provided <code>FindSpec</code> cares about distinct results.</p>
<p>I use the words &quot;cares about&quot; because find is generally defined in terms of producing distinct
results at the Datalog level.</p>
<p>Two of the find specs (scalar and tuple) produce only a single result. Those don't need to be
run with <code>SELECT DISTINCT</code>, because we're only consuming a single result. Those queries will be
run with <code>LIMIT 1</code>.</p>
<p>Additionally, some projections cannot produce duplicate results: <code>[:find (max ?x) …]</code>, for
example.</p>
<p>This function gives us the hook to add that logic when we're ready.</p>
<p>Beyond this, <code>DISTINCT</code> is not always needed. For example, in some kinds of accumulation or
sampling projections we might not need to do it at the SQL level because we're consuming into
a dupe-eliminating data structure like a Set, or we know that a particular query cannot produce
duplicate results.</p>
</div><h4 id='method.columns' class="method"><div class="important-traits"><div class='tooltip'>ⓘ<span class='tooltiptext'>Important traits for <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>&lt;R&gt;</span></div><div class="content hidden"><h3 class="important">Important traits for <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>&lt;R&gt;</h3><code class="content"><span class="where fmt-newline">impl&lt;R&gt; <a class="trait" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html" title="trait std::io::Write">Write</a> for <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>&lt;W&gt; <p>Callers are responsible for managing the memory for the return value.
The destructors <code>in_progress_destroy</code> and <code>tx_report_destroy</code> arew provided for
releasing the memory for these pointer types.</p>

</div>pub unsafe extern &quot;C&quot; fn store_begin_transaction&lt;'a, 'c&gt;(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;store: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="struct" href="../mentat_ffi/struct.Store.html" title="struct mentat_ffi::Store">Store</a>, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;error: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="struct" href="../mentat_ffi/utils/error/struct.ExternError.html" title="struct mentat_ffi::utils::error::ExternError">ExternError</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="struct" href="../mentat_ffi/struct.InProgress.html" title="struct mentat_ffi::InProgress">InProgress</a>&lt;'a, 'c&gt;</pre><div class='docblock'><p>Starts a new transaction to allow multiple transacts to be
performed together. This is more efficient than performing
a large set of individual commits.</p>
<h1 id="safety" class="section-header"><a href="#safety">Safety</a></h1>
<p>Callers must ensure that the pointer to the <a href="mentat::Store">Store</a> is not dangling.</p>
<p>Callers are responsible for managing the memory for the return value.
A destructor <code>in_progress_destroy</code> is provided for releasing the memory for this
pointer type.</p>

<code>store_cache_attribute_bi_directional</code> caches entity in both available directions, forward and reverse.</p>
<p><code>Forward</code> caches values for an attribute keyed by entity
(i.e. find values and entities that have this attribute, or find values of attribute for an entity)</p>
<p><code>Reverse</code> caches entities for an attribute keyed by value.
(i.e. find entities that have a particular value for an attribute).</p>

</div>pub extern &quot;C&quot; fn store_open(uri: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*const </a><a class="type" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/os/raw/type.c_char.html" title="type std::os::raw::c_char">c_char</a>) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="struct" href="../mentat_ffi/struct.Store.html" title="struct mentat_ffi::Store">Store</a></pre><div class='docblock'><p>A store cannot be opened twice to the same location.
Once created, the reference to the store is held by the caller and not Rust,
therefore the caller is responsible for calling <code>store_destroy</code> to release the memory
used by the <a href="mentat::Store">Store</a> in order to avoid a memory leak.</p>
<h1 id="safety" class="section-header"><a href="#safety">Safety</a></h1>
<p>Callers are responsible for managing the memory for the return value.
A destructor <code>store_destroy</code> is provided for releasing the memory for this
pointer type.</p>

</div>pub unsafe extern &quot;C&quot; fn typed_value_into_boolean(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;typed_value: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="enum" href="../mentat_ffi/enum.Binding.html" title="enum mentat_ffi::Binding">Binding</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html">i32</a></pre><div class='docblock'><p>Consumes a <a href="mentat::Binding">Binding</a> and returns the value as a boolean represented as an <code>i32</code>.

</div>pub unsafe extern &quot;C&quot; fn value_at_index_into_uuid(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;values: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_ffi/enum.Binding.html" title="enum mentat_ffi::Binding">Binding</a>&gt;, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;index: <a class="type" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/os/raw/type.c_int.html" title="type std::os::raw::c_int">c_int</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html">[</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html">u8</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html">; 16]</a></pre><div class='docblock'><p>Returns the value of the <a href="mentat::Binding">Binding</a> at <code>index</code> as a UUID byte slice of length 16.</p>
<h1 id="panics" class="section-header"><a href="#panics">Panics</a></h1>
<p>If the <a href="mentat::ValueType">ValueType</a> of the <a href="mentat::Binding">Binding</a> is not <a href="mentat::ValueType::Uuid">ValueType::Uuid</a>.
If there is no value at <code>index</code>.</p>

}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A C representation Rust's <a href="std::option::Option">Option</a>.
A value of <code>Some</code> results in <code>value</code> containing a raw pointer as a <code>c_void</code>.
A value of <code>None</code> results in <code>value</code> containing a null pointer.</p>
<p>#Safety</p>
<p>Callers are responsible for managing the memory for the return value.
A destructor <code>destroy</code> is provided for releasing the memory for this
pointer type.</p>

</div>pub struct ExternResult {
    pub ok: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*const </a><a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/os/raw/enum.c_void.html" title="enum std::os::raw::c_void">c_void</a>,
    pub err: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*const </a><a class="type" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/os/raw/type.c_char.html" title="type std::os::raw::c_char">c_char</a>,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A C representation Rust's <a href="std::result::Result">Result</a>.
A value of <code>Ok</code> results in <code>ok</code> containing a raw pointer as a <code>c_void</code>
and <code>err</code> containing a null pointer.
A value of <code>Err</code> results in <code>value</code> containing a null pointer and <code>err</code> containing an error message.</p>
<p>#Safety</p>
<p>Callers are responsible for managing the memory for the return value.
A destructor <code>destroy</code> is provided for releasing the memory for this
pointer type.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat_ffi</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>InProgress</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat/conn.rs.html#195-205' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct InProgress&lt;'a, 'c&gt; { /* fields omitted */ }</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Represents an in-progress, not yet committed, set of changes to the store.
Call <code>commit</code> to commit your changes, or <code>rollback</code> to discard them.
A transaction is held open until you do so.
Your changes will be implicitly dropped along with this struct.</p>
</div>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat_ffi</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>QueryInputs</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_query_algebrizer/clauses/inputs.rs.html#33-36' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct QueryInputs { /* fields omitted */ }</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Define the inputs to a query. This is in two parts: a set of values known now, and a set of
types known now.
The separate map of types is to allow queries to be algebrized without full knowledge of
the bindings that will be used at execution time.
When built correctly, <code>types</code> is guaranteed to contain the types of <code>values</code> -- use
<code>QueryInputs::new</code> or <code>QueryInputs::with_values</code> to construct an instance.</p>
</div>
                    <h2 id='methods' class='small-section-header'>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat_ffi</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>RelResult</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_query_projector/relresult.rs.html#35-38' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct RelResult&lt;T&gt; {
    pub width: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a>,
    pub values: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;T&gt;,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The result you get from a 'rel' query, like:</p>
<pre><code class="language-edn">[:find ?person ?name
 :where [?person :person/name ?name]]
</code></pre>
<p>There are three ways to get data out of a <code>RelResult</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li>By iterating over rows as slices. Use <code>result.rows()</code>. This is efficient and is
recommended in two cases:
<ol>
<li>If you don't need to take ownership of the resulting values (e.g., you're comparing
or making a modified clone).</li>
<li>When the data you're retrieving is cheap to clone. All scalar values are relatively
cheap: they're either small values or <code>Rc</code>.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>By direct reference to a row by index, using <code>result.row(i)</code>. This also returns
a reference.</li>
<li>By consuming the results using <code>into_iter</code>. This allocates short-lived vectors,
but gives you ownership of the enclosed <code>TypedValue</code>s.</li>
</ul>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.width" class="structfield small-section-header">

</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.tx_id" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.tx_id" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="tx_id.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>tx_id: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The transaction ID of the transaction.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.tx_instant" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.tx_instant" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="tx_instant.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>tx_instant: <a class="struct" href="https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.0/chrono/datetime/struct.DateTime.html" title="struct chrono::datetime::DateTime">DateTime</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.0/chrono/offset/utc/struct.Utc.html" title="struct chrono::offset::utc::Utc">Utc</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The timestamp when the transaction began to be committed.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.tempids" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.tempids" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="tempids.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>tempids: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>, <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A map from string literal tempid to resolved or allocated entid.</p>
<p>Every string literal tempid presented to the transactor either resolves via upsert to an
existing entid, or is allocated a new entid.  (It is possible for multiple distinct string
literal tempids to all unify to a single freshly allocated entid.)</p>

                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_core/types.rs.html#57' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><pre class='rust typedef'>type Entid = <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>;</pre><div class='docblock'><p>Represents one entid in the entid space.</p>
<p>Per https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html (see also http://stackoverflow.com/a/8499544), SQLite
stores signed integers up to 64 bits in size.  Since u32 is not appropriate for our use case, we
use i64 rather than manually truncating u64 to u63 and casting to i64 throughout the codebase.</p>
</div></section>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Function <a href='../../index.html'>mentat_ffi</a>::<wbr><a href='../index.html'>utils</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>error</a>::<wbr><a class="fn" href=''>translate_opt_result</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../../src/mentat_ffi/utils.rs.html#134-147' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><pre class='rust fn'>pub unsafe fn translate_opt_result&lt;T, E&gt;(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;result: <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;T&gt;, E&gt;, <br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;error: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="struct" href="../../../mentat_ffi/utils/error/struct.ExternError.html" title="struct mentat_ffi::utils::error::ExternError">ExternError</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut T</a> <span class="where fmt-newline">where<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;E: <a class="trait" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html" title="trait core::fmt::Display">Display</a>,&nbsp;</span></pre><div class='docblock'><p>Translate Result&lt;Option<T>, E&gt; into something C can understand, when T is not <code>#[repr(C)]</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li>If <code>result</code> is <code>Ok(Some(v))</code>, moves <code>v</code> to the heap and returns a pointer to it, and
sets <code>error</code> to a state indicating that no error occurred (<code>message</code> is null).</li>
<li>If <code>result</code> is <code>Ok(None)</code> returns a null pointer, but sets <code>error</code> to a state indicating
that no error occurred (<code>message</code> is null).</li>
<li>If <code>result</code> is <code>Err(e)</code>, returns a null pointer and stores a string representing the error
message (which was allocated on the heap and should eventually be freed) into
<code>error.message</code></li>
</ul>
</div></section>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../../index.html'>mentat_ffi</a>::<wbr><a href='../index.html'>utils</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>error</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>ExternError</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../../src/mentat_ffi/utils.rs.html#92-95' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'><div class="docblock attributes">#[repr(C)]
</div>pub struct ExternError {
    pub message: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html">*mut </a><a class="type" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/os/raw/type.c_char.html" title="type std::os::raw::c_char">c_char</a>,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Represents an error that occurred on the mentat side. Many mentat FFI functions take a
<code>*mut ExternError</code> as the last argument. This is an out parameter that indicates an
error that occurred during that function's execution (if any).</p>
<p>For functions that use this pattern, if the ExternError's message property is null, then no
error occurred. If the message is non-null then it contains a string description of the
error that occurred.</p>
<p>Important: This message is allocated on the heap and it is the consumer's responsibility to
free it using <code>destroy_mentat_string</code>!</p>
<p>While this pattern is not ergonomic in Rust, it offers two main benefits:</p>
<ol>
<li>It avoids defining a large number of <code>Result</code>-shaped types in the FFI consumer, as would
be required with something like an <code>struct ExternResult&lt;T&gt; { ok: *mut T, err:... }</code></li>
<li>It offers additional type safety over <code>struct ExternResult { ok: *mut c_void, err:... }</code>,
which helps avoid memory safety errors.</li>
</ol>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.message" class="structfield small-section-header">

                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat_parser_utils/value_and_span.rs.html#398-413' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><pre class='rust fn'>pub fn is_valid_keyword_map_k_v&lt;'a&gt;(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;(k, v): <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">(</a>&amp;'a <a class="struct" href="../../edn/types/struct.ValueAndSpan.html" title="struct edn::types::ValueAndSpan">ValueAndSpan</a>, &amp;'a <a class="struct" href="../../edn/types/struct.ValueAndSpan.html" title="struct edn::types::ValueAndSpan">ValueAndSpan</a><a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html">)</a><br>) -&gt; <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></pre><div class='docblock'><p>A <code>[k v]</code> pair in the map form of a keyword map must have the shape <code>[:k, [v1, v2, ...]]</code>, with
none of <code>v1</code>, <code>v2</code>, ... a keyword: without loss of generality, we cannot represent the case
where <code>vn</code> is a keyword <code>:l</code>, since <code>[:k v1 v2 ... :l]</code>, isn't a valid keyword map in vector
form.  This function tests that a <code>[k v]</code> pair obeys these constraints.</p>
<p>If we didn't test this, then we might flatten a map <code>[:k [:l]] to</code>[:k :l]`, which isn't a valid
keyword map in vector form.</p>
</div></section>

                           <td><a class="fn" href="fn.is_valid_keyword_map_k_v.html"
                                  title='fn mentat_parser_utils::value_and_span::is_valid_keyword_map_k_v'>is_valid_keyword_map_k_v</a></td>
                           <td class='docblock-short'>
                                <p>A <code>[k v]</code> pair in the map form of a keyword map must have the shape <code>[:k, [v1, v2, ...]]</code>, with
none of <code>v1</code>, <code>v2</code>, ... a keyword: without loss of generality, we cannot represent the case
where <code>vn</code> is a keyword <code>:l</code>, since <code>[:k v1 v2 ... :l]</code>, isn't a valid keyword map in vector
form.  This function tests that a <code>[k v]</code> pair obeys these constraints.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='../index.html'>mentat_parser_utils</a>::<wbr><a href='index.html'>value_and_span</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>OfExactly</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../../src/mentat_parser_utils/value_and_span.rs.html#208' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct OfExactly&lt;P, N&gt;(_, _);</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p><code>OfExactly</code> and <code>of_exactly</code> allow us to express nested parsers naturally.</p>
<p>For example, <code>vector().of_exactly(many(list()))</code> parses a vector-of-lists, like [(1 2) (:a :b) (&quot;test&quot;) ()].</p>
<p>The &quot;outer&quot; parser <code>P</code> and the &quot;nested&quot; parser <code>N</code> must be compatible: <code>P</code> must produce an
output <code>edn::ValueAndSpan</code> which can itself be turned into a stream of child elements; and <code>N</code>
must accept the resulting input <code>Stream</code>.  This compatibility allows us to lift errors from the
nested parser to the outer parser, which is part of what has made parsing <code>&amp;'a [edn::Value]</code>
difficult.</p>
</div>
