<span id="variant.NoBoundVariable" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.NoBoundVariable" class="anchor field"></a><span id='NoBoundVariable.v' class='invisible'><code>NoBoundVariable</code></span></span><span id="variant.UnexpectedBinding" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.UnexpectedBinding" class="anchor field"></a><span id='UnexpectedBinding.v' class='invisible'><code>UnexpectedBinding</code></span></span><span id="variant.RepeatedBoundVariable" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.RepeatedBoundVariable" class="anchor field"></a><span id='RepeatedBoundVariable.v' class='invisible'><code>RepeatedBoundVariable</code></span></span><span id="variant.ExpectedBindRel" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.ExpectedBindRel" class="anchor field"></a><span id='ExpectedBindRel.v' class='invisible'><code>ExpectedBindRel</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Expected <code>[[?x ?y]]</code> but got some other type of binding.  Mentat is deliberately more strict
than Datomic: we won't try to make sense of non-obvious (and potentially erroneous) bindings.</p>
</div><span id="variant.ExpectedBindRelOrBindColl" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.ExpectedBindRelOrBindColl" class="anchor field"></a><span id='ExpectedBindRelOrBindColl.v' class='invisible'><code>ExpectedBindRelOrBindColl</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Expected <code>[[?x ?y]]</code> or <code>[?x ...]</code> but got some other type of binding.  Mentat is
deliberately more strict than Datomic: we won't try to make sense of non-obvious (and
potentially erroneous) bindings.</p>
</div><span id="variant.InvalidNumberOfBindings" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.InvalidNumberOfBindings" class="anchor field"></a><span id='InvalidNumberOfBindings.v' class='invisible'><code>InvalidNumberOfBindings</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Expected <code>[?x1 … ?xN]</code> or <code>[[?x1 … ?xN]]</code> but got some other number of bindings.  Mentat is
deliberately more strict than Datomic: we prefer placeholders to omission.</p>

                                <p>Define the inputs to a query. This is in two parts: a set of values known now, and a set of
types known now.
The separate map of types is to allow queries to be algebrized without full knowledge of
the bindings that will be used at execution time.
When built correctly, <code>types</code> is guaranteed to contain the types of <code>values</code> -- use
<code>QueryInputs::new</code> or <code>QueryInputs::with_values</code> to construct an instance.</p>

    pub known_types: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>, <a class="struct" href="../mentat_core/value_type_set/struct.ValueTypeSet.html" title="struct mentat_core::value_type_set::ValueTypeSet">ValueTypeSet</a>&gt;,
    pub extracted_types: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>, <a class="struct" href="../mentat_query_algebrizer/struct.QualifiedAlias.html" title="struct mentat_query_algebrizer::QualifiedAlias">QualifiedAlias</a>&gt;,
    // some fields omitted
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>A <code>ConjoiningClauses</code> (CC) is a collection of clauses that are combined with <code>JOIN</code>.
The topmost form in a query is a <code>ConjoiningClauses</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li>Ordinary pattern clauses turn into <code>FROM</code> parts and <code>WHERE</code> parts using <code>=</code>.</li>
<li>Predicate clauses turn into the same, but with other functions.</li>
<li>Function clauses turn into <code>WHERE</code> parts using function-specific comparisons.</li>
<li><code>not</code> turns into <code>NOT EXISTS</code> with <code>WHERE</code> clauses inside the subquery to
bind it to the outer variables, or adds simple <code>WHERE</code> clauses to the outer
clause.</li>
<li><code>not-join</code> is similar, but with explicit binding.</li>
<li><code>or</code> turns into a collection of <code>UNION</code>s inside a subquery, or a simple
alternation.
<code>or</code>'s documentation states that all clauses must include the same vars,
but that's an over-simplification: all clauses must refer to the external
unification vars.
The entire <code>UNION</code>-set is <code>JOIN</code>ed to any surrounding expressions per the <code>rule-vars</code>
clause, or the intersection of the vars in the two sides of the <code>JOIN</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Not yet done:</p>
<ul>
<li>Function clauses with bindings turn into:
<ul>
<li>Subqueries. Perhaps less efficient? Certainly clearer.</li>
<li>Projection expressions, if only used for output.</li>
<li>Inline expressions?</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<hr />
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.empty_because" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.empty_because" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="empty_because.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>empty_because: <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_query_algebrizer/enum.EmptyBecause.html" title="enum mentat_query_algebrizer::EmptyBecause">EmptyBecause</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p><code>Some</code> if this set of clauses cannot yield results in the context of the current schema.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.from" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.from" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="from.v" class='invisible'>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A vector of source/alias pairs used to construct a SQL <code>FROM</code> list.</p>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A vector of computed tables (typically subqueries). The index into this vector is used as
an identifier in a <code>DatomsTable::Computed(c)</code> table reference.</p>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A map from var to qualified columns. Used to project.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.input_variables" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.input_variables" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="input_variables.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>input_variables: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/set/struct.BTreeSet.html" title="struct alloc::btree::set::BTreeSet">BTreeSet</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A list of variables mentioned in the enclosing query's :in clause. These must all be bound
before the query can be executed. TODO: clarify what this means for nested CCs.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.known_types" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.known_types" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="known_types.v" class='invisible'>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A map from var to type. Whenever a var maps unambiguously to two different types, it cannot
yield results, so we don't represent that case here. If a var isn't present in the map, it
means that its type is not known in advance.
Usually that state should be represented by <code>ValueTypeSet::Any</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.extracted_types" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.extracted_types" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="extracted_types.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>extracted_types: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html" title="struct alloc::btree::map::BTreeMap">BTreeMap</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>, <a class="struct" href="../mentat_query_algebrizer/struct.QualifiedAlias.html" title="struct mentat_query_algebrizer::QualifiedAlias">QualifiedAlias</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A mapping, similar to <code>column_bindings</code>, but used to pull type tags out of the store at runtime.
If a var isn't unit in <code>known_types</code>, it should be present here.</p>
</div>

                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Accepted types are: <code>fn</code>, <code>mod</code>,
                    <code>struct</code>, <code>enum</code>,
                    <code>trait</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>macro</code>,
                    and <code>const</code>.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Search functions by type signature (e.g.
                    <code>vec -> usize</code> or <code>* -> vec</code>)
                </p>

               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_query_algebrizer/clauses/inputs.rs.html#33-36' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct QueryInputs { /* fields omitted */ }</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Define the inputs to a query. This is in two parts: a set of values known now, and a set of
types known now.
The separate map of types is to allow queries to be algebrized without full knowledge of
the bindings that will be used at execution time.
When built correctly, <code>types</code> is guaranteed to contain the types of <code>values</code> -- use
<code>QueryInputs::new</code> or <code>QueryInputs::with_values</code> to construct an instance.</p>
</div>

<code>QueryResults</code>: SQL-related projection information (<code>DISTINCT</code>, columns, etc.) and

</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.sql_projection" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.sql_projection" class="anchor field"></a>

                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A SQL projection, mapping columns mentioned in the body of the query to columns in the
output.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.pre_aggregate_projection" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.pre_aggregate_projection" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="pre_aggregate_projection.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>pre_aggregate_projection: <a class="enum" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_query_sql/enum.Projection.html" title="enum mentat_query_sql::Projection">Projection</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>If a query contains aggregates, we need to generate a nested subquery: an inner query
that returns our distinct variable bindings (and any <code>:with</code> vars), and an outer query
that applies aggregation. That's so we can put <code>DISTINCT</code> in the inner query and apply
aggregation afterwards -- <code>SELECT DISTINCT count(foo)</code> counts <em>then</em> uniques, and we need
the opposite to implement Datalog distinct semantics.
If this is the case, <code>sql_projection</code> will be the outer query's projection list, and
<code>pre_aggregate_projection</code> will be the inner.
If the query doesn't use aggregation, this field will be <code>None</code>.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.datalog_projector" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.datalog_projector" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="datalog_projector.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>datalog_projector: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>&lt;<a class="trait" href="../mentat_query_projector/trait.Projector.html" title="trait mentat_query_projector::Projector">Projector</a>&gt;</code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>A Datalog projection. This consumes rows of the appropriate shape (as defined by
the SQL projection) to yield one of the four kinds of Datalog query result.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.distinct" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.distinct" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="distinct.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>distinct: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html">bool</a></code>
                           </span></span><div class='docblock'><p>True if this query requires the SQL query to include DISTINCT.</p>
</div><span id="structfield.group_by_cols" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.group_by_cols" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="group_by_cols.v" class='invisible'>

                           </span></span>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Struct <a href='index.html'>mentat_query_projector</a>::<wbr><a class="struct" href=''>RelResult</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span><a class='srclink' href='../src/mentat_query_projector/relresult.rs.html#35-38' title='goto source code'>[src]</a></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust struct'>pub struct RelResult&lt;T&gt; {
    pub width: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a>,
    pub values: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;T&gt;,
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>The result you get from a 'rel' query, like:</p>
<pre><code class="language-edn">[:find ?person ?name
 :where [?person :person/name ?name]]
</code></pre>
<p>There are three ways to get data out of a <code>RelResult</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li>By iterating over rows as slices. Use <code>result.rows()</code>. This is efficient and is
recommended in two cases:
<ol>
<li>If you don't need to take ownership of the resulting values (e.g., you're comparing
or making a modified clone).</li>
<li>When the data you're retrieving is cheap to clone. All scalar values are relatively
cheap: they're either small values or <code>Rc</code>.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>By direct reference to a row by index, using <code>result.row(i)</code>. This also returns
a reference.</li>
<li>By consuming the results using <code>into_iter</code>. This allocates short-lived vectors,
but gives you ownership of the enclosed <code>TypedValue</code>s.</li>
</ul>
</div><h2 id='fields' class='fields small-section-header'>
                       Fields<a href='#fields' class='anchor'></a></h2><span id="structfield.width" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.width" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="width.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>width: <a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html">usize</a></code>
                           </span></span><span id="structfield.values" class="structfield small-section-header">
                           <a href="#structfield.values" class="anchor field"></a>
                           <span id="values.v" class='invisible'>
                           <code>values: <a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;T&gt;</code>

}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>One of the things that can appear in a projection or a constraint. Note that we use
<code>TypedValue</code> here; it's not pure SQL, but it avoids us having to concern ourselves at this
point with the translation between a <code>TypedValue</code> and the storage-layer representation.</p>
<p>Eventually we might allow different translations by providing a different <code>QueryBuilder</code>
implementation for each storage backend. Passing <code>TypedValue</code>s here allows for that.</p>

                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Accepted types are: <code>fn</code>, <code>mod</code>,
                    <code>struct</code>, <code>enum</code>,
                    <code>trait</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>macro</code>,
                    and <code>const</code>.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Search functions by type signature (e.g.
                    <code>vec -> usize</code> or <code>* -> vec</code>)
                </p>
            </div>

</div><span id="variant.Named" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.Named" class="anchor field"></a><span id='Named.v' class='invisible'><code>Named(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="struct" href="../edn/query/struct.Variable.html" title="struct edn::query::Variable">Variable</a>&gt;,&nbsp;<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="enum" href="../mentat_core/types/enum.TypedValue.html" title="enum mentat_core::types::TypedValue">TypedValue</a>&gt;)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>Like &quot;SELECT 0 AS x, SELECT 0 AS y WHERE 0 UNION ALL VALUES (0, 1), (2, 3), ...&quot;.

of the vector of names.</p>

    <section id='main' class="content"><h1 class='fqn'><span class='in-band'>Enum <a href='index.html'>mentat_sql</a>::<wbr><a class="enum" href=''>Value</a></span><span class='out-of-band'><span id='render-detail'>
                   <a id="toggle-all-docs" href="javascript:void(0)" title="collapse all docs">
                       [<span class='inner'>&#x2212;</span>]
                   </a>
               </span></span></h1><div class="docblock type-decl"><pre class='rust enum'>pub enum Value {
    Null,
    Integer(<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>),
    Real(<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html">f64</a>),
    Text(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>),
    Blob(<a class="struct" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>&lt;<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html">u8</a>&gt;),
}</pre></div><div class='docblock'><p>Owning <a href="http://sqlite.org/datatype3.html">dynamic type value</a>. Value's type is typically
dictated by SQLite (not by the caller).</p>
<p>See <a href="enum.ValueRef.html"><code>ValueRef</code></a> for a non-owning dynamic type value.</p>
</div><h2 id='variants' class='variants small-section-header'>

</div><span id="variant.Integer" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.Integer" class="anchor field"></a><span id='Integer.v' class='invisible'><code>Integer(<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html">i64</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The value is a signed integer.</p>
</div><span id="variant.Real" class="variant small-section-header"><a href="#variant.Real" class="anchor field"></a><span id='Real.v' class='invisible'><code>Real(<a class="primitive" href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html">f64</a>)</code></span></span><div class='docblock'><p>The value is a floating point number.</p>

                           <td class='docblock-short'>

This struct encapsulates the generated string and the <em>initial</em> argument list.
Additional user-supplied argument bindings, with their placeholders accumulated via
<code>push_bind_param</code>, will be appended to this argument list.</p>

<span class="doccomment">//! This module defines core types that support the transaction processor.</span>

<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">std</span>::<span class="ident">collections</span>::<span class="ident">BTreeMap</span>;
<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">std</span>::<span class="ident">fmt</span>;

<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">symbols</span>::{
    <span class="ident">Keyword</span>,
    <span class="ident">PlainSymbol</span>,

<span class="doccomment">/// A tempid, either an external tempid given in a transaction (usually as an `Value::Text`),</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// or an internal tempid allocated by Mentat itself.</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">enum</span> <span class="ident">TempId</span> {
    <span class="ident">External</span>(<span class="ident">String</span>),
    <span class="ident">Internal</span>(<span class="ident">i64</span>),
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">TempId</span> {
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">into_external</span>(<span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-ty">Option</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">String</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="kw">match</span> <span class="self">self</span> {
            <span class="ident">TempId</span>::<span class="ident">External</span>(<span class="ident">s</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-val">Some</span>(<span class="ident">s</span>),
            <span class="ident">TempId</span>::<span class="ident">Internal</span>(<span class="kw">_</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-val">None</span>,
        }
    }
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">fmt</span>::<span class="ident">Display</span> <span class="kw">for</span> <span class="ident">TempId</span> {
    <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">fmt</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>, <span class="ident">f</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="kw-2">mut</span> <span class="ident">fmt</span>::<span class="ident">Formatter</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-ty">Result</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>(), <span class="ident">fmt</span>::<span class="ident">Error</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="kw">match</span> <span class="self">self</span> {
            <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">TempId</span>::<span class="ident">External</span>(<span class="kw-2">ref</span> <span class="ident">s</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="macro">write</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">f</span>, <span class="string">&quot;{}&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">s</span>),
            <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">TempId</span>::<span class="ident">Internal</span>(<span class="ident">x</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="macro">write</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="ident">f</span>, <span class="string">&quot;&lt;tempid {}&gt;&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">x</span>),
        }
    }
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">enum</span> <span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span> {
    <span class="ident">Entid</span>(<span class="ident">i64</span>),
    <span class="ident">Ident</span>(<span class="ident">Keyword</span>),
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span> {
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">unreversed</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-ty">Option</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="kw">match</span> <span class="self">self</span> {
            <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span>::<span class="ident">Entid</span>(<span class="kw">_</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-val">None</span>,
            <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span>::<span class="ident">Ident</span>(<span class="kw-2">ref</span> <span class="ident">a</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="ident">a</span>.<span class="ident">unreversed</span>().<span class="ident">map</span>(<span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span>::<span class="ident">Ident</span>),
        }
    }
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">struct</span> <span class="ident">LookupRef</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="ident">a</span>: <span class="ident">AttributePlace</span>,
    <span class="comment">// In theory we could allow nested lookup-refs.  In practice this would require us to process</span>
    <span class="comment">// lookup-refs in multiple phases, like how we resolve tempids, which isn&#39;t worth the effort.</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="ident">v</span>: <span class="ident">V</span>, <span class="comment">// An atom.</span>
}

<span class="doccomment">/// A &quot;transaction function&quot; that exposes some value determined by the current transaction.  The</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// prototypical example is the current transaction ID, `(transaction-tx)`.</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// A natural next step might be to expose the current transaction instant `(transaction-instant)`,</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// but that&#39;s more difficult: the transaction itself can set the transaction instant (with some</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// restrictions), so the transaction function must be late-binding.  Right now, that&#39;s difficult to</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// arrange in the transactor.</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// In the future, we might accept arguments; for example, perhaps we might expose `(ancestor</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// (transaction-tx) n)` to find the n-th ancestor of the current transaction.  If we do accept</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// arguments, then the special case of `(lookup-ref a v)` should be handled as part of the</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// generalization.</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">struct</span> <span class="ident">TxFunction</span> {
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="ident">op</span>: <span class="ident">PlainSymbol</span>,
}

<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">type</span> <span class="ident">MapNotation</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">BTreeMap</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span>, <span class="ident">ValuePlace</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;&gt;</span>;

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">enum</span> <span class="ident">ValuePlace</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
    <span class="comment">// We never know at parse-time whether an integer or ident is really an entid, but we will often</span>
    <span class="comment">// know when building entities programmatically.</span>
    <span class="ident">Entid</span>(<span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span>),
    <span class="comment">// We never know at parse-time whether a string is really a tempid, but we will often know when</span>
    <span class="comment">// building entities programmatically.</span>
    <span class="ident">TempId</span>(<span class="ident">TempId</span>),
    <span class="ident">LookupRef</span>(<span class="ident">LookupRef</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>),
    <span class="ident">TxFunction</span>(<span class="ident">TxFunction</span>),
    <span class="ident">Vector</span>(<span class="ident">Vec</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">ValuePlace</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;&gt;</span>),
    <span class="ident">Atom</span>(<span class="ident">V</span>),
    <span class="ident">MapNotation</span>(<span class="ident">MapNotation</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>),
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">enum</span> <span class="ident">EntityPlace</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
    <span class="ident">Entid</span>(<span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span>),
    <span class="ident">TempId</span>(<span class="ident">TempId</span>),
    <span class="ident">LookupRef</span>(<span class="ident">LookupRef</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>),
    <span class="ident">TxFunction</span>(<span class="ident">TxFunction</span>),
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">enum</span> <span class="ident">AttributePlace</span> {
    <span class="ident">Entid</span>(<span class="ident">EntidOrIdent</span>),
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Copy</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">enum</span> <span class="ident">OpType</span> {
    <span class="ident">Add</span>,
    <span class="ident">Retract</span>,
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Debug</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">Ord</span>, <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">enum</span> <span class="ident">Entity</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
    <span class="comment">// Like [:db/add|:db/retract e a v].</span>
    <span class="ident">AddOrRetract</span> {
        <span class="ident">op</span>: <span class="ident">OpType</span>,
        <span class="ident">e</span>: <span class="ident">EntityPlace</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>,
        <span class="ident">a</span>: <span class="ident">AttributePlace</span>,
        <span class="ident">v</span>: <span class="ident">ValuePlace</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>,
    },
    <span class="comment">// Like {:db/id &quot;tempid&quot; a1 v1 a2 v2}.</span>
    <span class="ident">MapNotation</span>(<span class="ident">MapNotation</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">V</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>),
}

<span class="comment">// Copyright 2018 Mozilla</span>

<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">std</span>::<span class="ident">cmp</span>::{
    <span class="ident">Ord</span>,
    <span class="ident">Ordering</span>,
    <span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>,
};

<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">std</span>::<span class="ident">fmt</span>;

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">cfg</span>(<span class="ident">feature</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;serde_support&quot;</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">use</span> <span class="ident">serde</span>::<span class="ident">de</span>::{
    <span class="self">self</span>,
    <span class="ident">Deserialize</span>,

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">cfg</span>(<span class="ident">feature</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;serde_support&quot;</span>)]</span>

    <span class="ident">Serialize</span>,
    <span class="ident">Serializer</span>,
};

<span class="comment">// Data storage for both NamespaceableKeyword and NamespaceableSymbol.</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>, <span class="ident">Eq</span>, <span class="ident">Hash</span>, <span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">struct</span> <span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span> {
    <span class="comment">// The bytes that make up the namespace followed directly by those</span>
    <span class="comment">// that make up the name. If there is a namespace, a solidus (&#39;/&#39;) is between</span>
    <span class="comment">// the two parts.</span>
    <span class="ident">components</span>: <span class="ident">String</span>,

    <span class="comment">// The index (in bytes) into `components` of the dividing solidus — the character</span>
    <span class="comment">// between the namespace and the name.</span>
    <span class="comment">//</span>
    <span class="comment">// If this is zero, it means that this is _not_ a namespaced value!</span>
    <span class="comment">//</span>
    <span class="comment">// Important: The following invariants around `boundary` must be maintained:</span>
    <span class="comment">//</span>
    <span class="comment">// 1. `boundary` must always be less than or equal to `components.len()`.</span>
    <span class="comment">// 2. `boundary` must be a byte index that points to a character boundary,</span>
    <span class="comment">//     and not point into the middle of a UTF-8 codepoint. That is,</span>
    <span class="comment">//    `components.is_char_boundary(boundary)` must always be true.</span>
    <span class="comment">//</span>
    <span class="comment">// These invariants are enforced by `NamespaceableName::namespaced()`, and since</span>
    <span class="comment">// we never mutate `NamespaceableName`s, that&#39;s the only place we need to</span>
    <span class="comment">// worry about them.</span>
    <span class="ident">boundary</span>: <span class="ident">usize</span>,
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span> {
    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">plain</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">T</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="ident">name</span>: <span class="ident">T</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="self">Self</span> <span class="kw">where</span> <span class="ident">T</span>: <span class="ident">Into</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">String</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {

<span class="comment">// We order by namespace then by name.</span>
<span class="comment">// Non-namespaced values always sort before.</span>

    <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">partial_cmp</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>, <span class="ident">other</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-ty">Option</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">Ordering</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {

            (<span class="number">0</span>, <span class="number">0</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="ident">components</span>.<span class="ident">partial_cmp</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">other</span>.<span class="ident">components</span>),
            (<span class="number">0</span>, <span class="kw">_</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-val">Some</span>(<span class="ident">Ordering</span>::<span class="ident">Less</span>),

            (<span class="kw">_</span>, <span class="kw">_</span>) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> {
                <span class="comment">// Just use a lexicographic ordering.</span>
                <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="ident">components</span>().<span class="ident">partial_cmp</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">other</span>.<span class="ident">components</span>())
            },
        }
    }

<span class="comment">// This is convoluted, but the basic idea is that since we don&#39;t want to rely on our input being</span>
<span class="comment">// correct, we&#39;ll need to implement a custom serializer no matter what (e.g. we can&#39;t just</span>
<span class="comment">// `derive(Deserialize)` since `unsafe` code depends on `self.boundary` being a valid index).</span>
<span class="comment">//</span>
<span class="comment">// We&#39;d also like for users consuming our serialized data as e.g. JSON not to have to learn how we</span>
<span class="comment">// store NamespaceableName internally, since it&#39;s very much an implementation detail.</span>
<span class="comment">//</span>
<span class="comment">// We achieve both of these by implemeting a type that can serialize in way that&#39;s both user-</span>
<span class="comment">// friendly and automatic (e.g. `derive`d), and just pass all work off to it in our custom</span>
<span class="comment">// implementation of Serialize and Deserialize.</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">cfg</span>(<span class="ident">feature</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;serde_support&quot;</span>)]</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">cfg_attr</span>(<span class="ident">feature</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;serde_support&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">serde</span>(<span class="ident">rename</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;NamespaceableName&quot;</span>))]</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">cfg_attr</span>(<span class="ident">feature</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;serde_support&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Serialize</span>, <span class="ident">Deserialize</span>))]</span>
<span class="kw">struct</span> <span class="ident">SerializedNamespaceableName</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
    <span class="ident">namespace</span>: <span class="prelude-ty">Option</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="ident">str</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>,
    <span class="ident">name</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="ident">str</span>,
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">cfg</span>(<span class="ident">feature</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;serde_support&quot;</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">impl</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;de</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="ident">Deserialize</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;de</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="kw">for</span> <span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span> {

            <span class="kw">return</span> <span class="prelude-val">Err</span>(<span class="ident">de</span>::<span class="ident">Error</span>::<span class="ident">custom</span>(<span class="string">&quot;Empty name in keyword or symbol&quot;</span>));

<span class="doccomment">/// A simplification of Clojure&#39;s Symbol.</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>,<span class="ident">Debug</span>,<span class="ident">Eq</span>,<span class="ident">Hash</span>,<span class="ident">Ord</span>,<span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>,<span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">struct</span> <span class="ident">PlainSymbol</span>(<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="ident">String</span>);

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>,<span class="ident">Debug</span>,<span class="ident">Eq</span>,<span class="ident">Hash</span>,<span class="ident">Ord</span>,<span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>,<span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">struct</span> <span class="ident">NamespacedSymbol</span>(<span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span>);

<span class="doccomment">/// A keyword is a symbol, optionally with a namespace, that prints with a leading colon.</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// This concept is imported from Clojure, as it features in EDN and the query</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// syntax that we use.</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// Clojure&#39;s constraints are looser than ours, allowing empty namespaces or</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// names:</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// ```clojure</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// user=&gt; (keyword &quot;&quot; &quot;&quot;)</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// :/</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// user=&gt; (keyword &quot;foo&quot; &quot;&quot;)</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// :foo/</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// user=&gt; (keyword &quot;&quot; &quot;bar&quot;)</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// :/bar</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// We think that&#39;s nonsense, so we only allow keywords like `:bar` and `:foo/bar`,</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// with both namespace and main parts containing no whitespace and no colon or slash:</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::Keyword;</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// let bar     = Keyword::plain(&quot;bar&quot;);                         // :bar</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// let foo_bar = Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;bar&quot;);        // :foo/bar</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;bar&quot;, bar.name());</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(None, bar.namespace());</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;bar&quot;, foo_bar.name());</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(Some(&quot;foo&quot;), foo_bar.namespace());</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// If you&#39;re not sure whether your input is well-formed, you should use a</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// parser or a reader function first to validate. TODO: implement `read`.</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// Callers are expected to follow these rules:</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// http://www.clojure.org/reference/reader#_symbols</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// Future: fast equality (interning?) for keywords.</span>
<span class="doccomment">///</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Clone</span>,<span class="ident">Debug</span>,<span class="ident">Eq</span>,<span class="ident">Hash</span>,<span class="ident">Ord</span>,<span class="ident">PartialOrd</span>,<span class="ident">PartialEq</span>)]</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">cfg_attr</span>(<span class="ident">feature</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="string">&quot;serde_support&quot;</span>, <span class="ident">derive</span>(<span class="ident">Serialize</span>, <span class="ident">Deserialize</span>))]</span>
<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">struct</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span>(<span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span>);

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">PlainSymbol</span> {
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">plain</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">T</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="ident">name</span>: <span class="ident">T</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="self">Self</span> <span class="kw">where</span> <span class="ident">T</span>: <span class="ident">Into</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">String</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">n</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">name</span>.<span class="ident">into</span>();
        <span class="macro">assert</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="op">!</span><span class="ident">n</span>.<span class="ident">is_empty</span>(), <span class="string">&quot;Symbols cannot be unnamed.&quot;</span>);

        <span class="ident">PlainSymbol</span>(<span class="ident">n</span>)
    }

    <span class="doccomment">/// Return the name of the symbol without any leading &#39;?&#39; or &#39;$&#39;.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::PlainSymbol;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;foo&quot;, PlainSymbol::plain(&quot;?foo&quot;).name());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;foo&quot;, PlainSymbol::plain(&quot;$foo&quot;).name());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;!foo&quot;, PlainSymbol::plain(&quot;!foo&quot;).name());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">name</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">str</span> {
        <span class="kw">if</span> <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="ident">is_src_symbol</span>() <span class="op">||</span> <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="ident">is_var_symbol</span>() {
            <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>[<span class="number">1</span>..]
        } <span class="kw">else</span> {
            <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>
        }
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">is_var_symbol</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="ident">bool</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">starts_with</span>(<span class="string">&#39;?&#39;</span>)
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">is_src_symbol</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="ident">bool</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">starts_with</span>(<span class="string">&#39;$&#39;</span>)
    }
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">NamespacedSymbol</span> {
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">namespaced</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">N</span>, <span class="ident">T</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="ident">namespace</span>: <span class="ident">N</span>, <span class="ident">name</span>: <span class="ident">T</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="self">Self</span> <span class="kw">where</span> <span class="ident">N</span>: <span class="ident">AsRef</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">str</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>, <span class="ident">T</span>: <span class="ident">AsRef</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">str</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">r</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">namespace</span>.<span class="ident">as_ref</span>();
        <span class="macro">assert</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="op">!</span><span class="ident">r</span>.<span class="ident">is_empty</span>(), <span class="string">&quot;Namespaced symbols cannot have an empty non-null namespace.&quot;</span>);
        <span class="ident">NamespacedSymbol</span>(<span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span>::<span class="ident">namespaced</span>(<span class="ident">r</span>, <span class="ident">name</span>))
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">name</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">str</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">name</span>()
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">namespace</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">str</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">namespace</span>().<span class="ident">unwrap</span>()
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">components</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> (<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="ident">str</span>, <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="ident">str</span>) {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">components</span>()
    }
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span> {
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">plain</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">T</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="ident">name</span>: <span class="ident">T</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="self">Self</span> <span class="kw">where</span> <span class="ident">T</span>: <span class="ident">Into</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">String</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="ident">Keyword</span>(<span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span>::<span class="ident">plain</span>(<span class="ident">name</span>))
    }
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span> {
    <span class="doccomment">/// Creates a new `Keyword`.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::Keyword;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// let keyword = Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;bar&quot;);</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(keyword.to_string(), &quot;:foo/bar&quot;);</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// See also the `kw!` macro in the main `mentat` crate.</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">namespaced</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">N</span>, <span class="ident">T</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="ident">namespace</span>: <span class="ident">N</span>, <span class="ident">name</span>: <span class="ident">T</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="self">Self</span> <span class="kw">where</span> <span class="ident">N</span>: <span class="ident">AsRef</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">str</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>, <span class="ident">T</span>: <span class="ident">AsRef</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">str</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="kw">let</span> <span class="ident">r</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="ident">namespace</span>.<span class="ident">as_ref</span>();
        <span class="macro">assert</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="op">!</span><span class="ident">r</span>.<span class="ident">is_empty</span>(), <span class="string">&quot;Namespaced keywords cannot have an empty non-null namespace.&quot;</span>);
        <span class="ident">Keyword</span>(<span class="ident">NamespaceableName</span>::<span class="ident">namespaced</span>(<span class="ident">r</span>, <span class="ident">name</span>))
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">name</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">str</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">name</span>()
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">namespace</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-ty">Option</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">str</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">namespace</span>()
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">components</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> (<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="ident">str</span>, <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="lifetime">&#39;a</span> <span class="ident">str</span>) {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">components</span>()
    }

    <span class="doccomment">/// Whether this `Keyword` should be interpreted in reverse order. For example,</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// the two following snippets are identical:</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```edn</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// [?y :person/friend ?x]</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// [?x :person/hired ?y]</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// [?y :person/friend ?x]</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// [?y :person/_hired ?x]</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::Keyword;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert!(!Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;bar&quot;).is_backward());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert!(Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;_bar&quot;).is_backward());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">is_backward</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="ident">bool</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">is_backward</span>()
    }

    <span class="doccomment">/// Whether this `Keyword` should be interpreted in forward order.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// See `symbols::Keyword::is_backward`.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::Keyword;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert!(Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;bar&quot;).is_forward());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert!(!Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;_bar&quot;).is_forward());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">is_forward</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="ident">bool</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">is_forward</span>()
    }

    <span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">inline</span>]</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">is_namespaced</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="ident">bool</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">is_namespaced</span>()
    }

    <span class="doccomment">/// Returns a `Keyword` with the same namespace and a</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// &#39;backward&#39; name. See `symbols::Keyword::is_backward`.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// Returns a forward name if passed a reversed keyword; i.e., this</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// function is its own inverse.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::Keyword;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// let nsk = Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;bar&quot;);</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert!(!nsk.is_backward());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;:foo/bar&quot;, nsk.to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// let reversed = nsk.to_reversed();</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert!(reversed.is_backward());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;:foo/_bar&quot;, reversed.to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">to_reversed</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span> {
        <span class="ident">Keyword</span>(<span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">to_reversed</span>())
    }

    <span class="doccomment">/// If this `Keyword` is &#39;backward&#39; (see `symbols::Keyword::is_backward`),</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// return `Some(&#39;forward name&#39;)`; otherwise, return `None`.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::Keyword;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// let nsk = Keyword::namespaced(&quot;foo&quot;, &quot;bar&quot;);</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(None, nsk.unreversed());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// let reversed = nsk.to_reversed();</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(Some(nsk), reversed.unreversed());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">unreversed</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-ty">Option</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">Keyword</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
        <span class="kw">if</span> <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="ident">is_backward</span>() {
            <span class="prelude-val">Some</span>(<span class="self">self</span>.<span class="ident">to_reversed</span>())
        } <span class="kw">else</span> {
            <span class="prelude-val">None</span>
        }
    }
}

<span class="comment">//</span>
<span class="comment">// Note that we don&#39;t currently do any escaping.</span>
<span class="comment">//</span>

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">Display</span> <span class="kw">for</span> <span class="ident">PlainSymbol</span> {
    <span class="doccomment">/// Print the symbol in EDN format.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::PlainSymbol;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;baz&quot;, PlainSymbol::plain(&quot;baz&quot;).to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">fmt</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>, <span class="ident">f</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="kw-2">mut</span> <span class="ident">Formatter</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> ::<span class="ident">std</span>::<span class="ident">fmt</span>::<span class="prelude-ty">Result</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">fmt</span>(<span class="ident">f</span>)
    }
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">Display</span> <span class="kw">for</span> <span class="ident">NamespacedSymbol</span> {
    <span class="doccomment">/// Print the symbol in EDN format.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::NamespacedSymbol;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;bar/baz&quot;, NamespacedSymbol::namespaced(&quot;bar&quot;, &quot;baz&quot;).to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">fmt</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>, <span class="ident">f</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="kw-2">mut</span> <span class="ident">Formatter</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> ::<span class="ident">std</span>::<span class="ident">fmt</span>::<span class="prelude-ty">Result</span> {
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">fmt</span>(<span class="ident">f</span>)
    }
}

<span class="kw">impl</span> <span class="ident">Display</span> <span class="kw">for</span> <span class="ident">Keyword</span> {
    <span class="doccomment">/// Print the keyword in EDN format.</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # Examples</span>
    <span class="doccomment">///</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```rust</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// # use edn::symbols::Keyword;</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;:baz&quot;, Keyword::plain(&quot;baz&quot;).to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;:bar/baz&quot;, Keyword::namespaced(&quot;bar&quot;, &quot;baz&quot;).to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;:bar/_baz&quot;, Keyword::namespaced(&quot;bar&quot;, &quot;baz&quot;).to_reversed().to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// assert_eq!(&quot;:bar/baz&quot;, Keyword::namespaced(&quot;bar&quot;, &quot;baz&quot;).to_reversed().to_reversed().to_string());</span>
    <span class="doccomment">/// ```</span>
    <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">fmt</span>(<span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="self">self</span>, <span class="ident">f</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="kw-2">mut</span> <span class="ident">Formatter</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> ::<span class="ident">std</span>::<span class="ident">fmt</span>::<span class="prelude-ty">Result</span> {
        <span class="ident">f</span>.<span class="ident">write_char</span>(<span class="string">&#39;:&#39;</span>)<span class="question-mark">?</span>;
        <span class="self">self</span>.<span class="number">0</span>.<span class="ident">fmt</span>(<span class="ident">f</span>)
    }
}

<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">test</span>]</span>
<span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">test_ns_keyword_macro</span>() {
    <span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro">ns_keyword</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;test&quot;</span>, <span class="string">&quot;name&quot;</span>).<span class="ident">to_string</span>(),

    <span class="macro">assert_eq</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro">ns_keyword</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;ns&quot;</span>, <span class="string">&quot;_name&quot;</span>).<span class="ident">to_string</span>(),

<span class="kw">pub</span> <span class="kw">fn</span> <span class="ident">merge</span>(<span class="ident">left</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">Value</span>, <span class="ident">right</span>: <span class="kw-2">&amp;</span><span class="ident">Value</span>) <span class="op">-&gt;</span> <span class="prelude-ty">Option</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="ident">Value</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> {
    <span class="kw">match</span> (<span class="ident">left</span>, <span class="ident">right</span>) {

                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>

                    <code>struct</code>, <code>enum</code>,
                    <code>trait</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>macro</code>,
                    and <code>const</code>.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Search functions by type signature (e.g.
                    <code>vec -> usize</code> or <code>* -> vec</code>)
                </p>

<span class="doccomment">/// Produce the appropriate `Variable` for the provided valid ?-prefixed name.</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// This lives here because we can&#39;t re-export macros:</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/29638.</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">macro_export</span>]</span>
<span class="macro">macro_rules</span><span class="macro">!</span> <span class="ident">var</span> {
    ( <span class="question-mark">?</span> <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">var</span>:<span class="ident">ident</span> ) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> {
        <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="kw">crate</span>::<span class="macro-nonterminal">Variable</span>::<span class="ident">from_valid_name</span>(<span class="macro">concat</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="string">&quot;?&quot;</span>, <span class="macro">stringify</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">var</span>)))
    };
}

<span class="doccomment">/// Produce the appropriate `Keyword` for the provided namespace and name.</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// This lives here because we can&#39;t re-export macros:</span>
<span class="doccomment">/// https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/29638.</span>
<span class="attribute">#[<span class="ident">macro_export</span>]</span>
<span class="macro">macro_rules</span><span class="macro">!</span> <span class="ident">kw</span> {
    ( : <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">n</span>:<span class="ident">ident</span> ) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> {
        <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="kw">crate</span>::<span class="macro-nonterminal">Keyword</span>::<span class="ident">plain</span>(
            <span class="macro">stringify</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">n</span>)
        )
    };

    ( : <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">ns</span>:<span class="ident">ident</span> <span class="op">/</span> <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">n</span>:<span class="ident">ident</span> ) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> {
        <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="kw">crate</span>::<span class="macro-nonterminal">Keyword</span>::<span class="ident">namespaced</span>(
            <span class="macro">stringify</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">ns</span>),
            <span class="macro">stringify</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">n</span>)
        )
    };

    ( : <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">ns</span>:<span class="ident">ident</span>$(. <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">nss</span>:<span class="ident">ident</span>)<span class="op">+</span> <span class="op">/</span> <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">n</span>:<span class="ident">ident</span> ) <span class="op">=&gt;</span> {
        <span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="kw">crate</span>::<span class="macro-nonterminal">Keyword</span>::<span class="ident">namespaced</span>(
            <span class="macro">concat</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro">stringify</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">ns</span>) $(, <span class="string">&quot;.&quot;</span>, <span class="macro">stringify</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">nss</span>))<span class="op">+</span>),
            <span class="macro">stringify</span><span class="macro">!</span>(<span class="macro-nonterminal">$</span><span class="macro-nonterminal">n</span>)
        )
    };
}

            <div class="infos">
                <h2>Search Tricks</h2>

                <p>
                    Prefix searches with a type followed by a colon (e.g.
                    <code>fn:</code>) to restrict the search to a given type.
                </p>

                <p>
                    Accepted types are: <code>fn</code>, <code>mod</code>,
                    <code>struct</code>, <code>enum</code>,
                    <code>trait</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>macro</code>,
